items.title: KOLONİ
items.text:
KOLONİ is an agent workspace that runs on your own machine. You chat with an agent, the Orchestrator, in a folder of yours. It reads, searches, edits and runs commands there. It hands parts of the job to other agents (Coder, Reviewer, Tester and more) when that helps. The agents run on models you add: an API key, a model server of your own, or a CLI you are signed in to (Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot CLI, Qoder, agy). A canvas beside the chat draws each turn from what really happened. Before anything risky, an agent asks you on a card.

KOLONİ listens only on 127.0.0.1, on your own machine. It sends no telemetry.

KOLONİ's words and how they hang together. Each is explained in the Glossary.

items.title: Backup and update
items.text: What is where, what the update script does in order, and what Export and Restore cover. (full size)

items.title: Backups KOLONİ makes by itself
items.text:
Before a new version changes the database, KOLONİ copies it to runtime/data/backups/. It keeps the last five copies. The update script's own backup goes in the same folder and counts among those five.

Backups hold your API keys, in plain text, like the database itself. Keep runtime/ private.

items.title: Export everything
items.text:
Settings › The app › Your data › Export: "Everything KOLONİ keeps, in one .zip: chats, agents, providers, memory, triggers, skills and attachments. Your project folders stay where they are."

Not in the file: your project folders (with their .koloni/ folders and Knowledge), working copies, logs, and the CLIs' own sign-ins.

  • Include API keys and secrets (keep this file safe): without it, the keys KOLONİ stores in its settings are left out, and so are secret files you attached to a chat (a .env, a key file: the chat keeps their name, and the page lists them once you choose the file to restore). A key that was ever written in a chat, in another file you attached, an agent's output or a command stays in the file either way.
  • Export everything downloads the file.

items.title: Restore
items.text:
"Restore only a file you exported yourself: it decides which programs KOLONİ may start."

  1. Settings › The app › Your data › Restore from a file…, and choose the .zip.
  2. Nothing changes yet. Close KOLONİ and start it again; the restore happens at that start. Until then you can Cancel it.
  3. Your data as it was is set aside in runtime/before-restore/, not deleted.
  4. "Triggers and backlogs wait until you press Resume."

If the file had no keys, the page lists what needs its key again. A restore is refused while a turn is at work, or if the file is not a KOLONİ export, comes from a newer KOLONİ, or is damaged. If a restore fails at the start, your old data is put back, and the page says so.

items.title: Updating
items.text:
Stop KOLONİ first (Ctrl+C in its window). Then, in its folder:

Windows (PowerShell)macOS and Linux 
./scripts/update.ps1

./scripts/update.sh

It refuses if the folder is not a git checkout, if you have uncommitted changes in KOLONİ's files, or if something answers on KOLONİ's port. Otherwise, in order:

  1. backs up the database to runtime/data/backups/;
  2. pulls the new version (git pull --ff-only);
  3. updates the Python packages;
  4. updates the page's packages and builds the page;
  5. where Zensical is installed, rebuilds this guide (see This guide inside KOLONİ).

It stops at the first step that fails: "nothing after it ran". Only the guide's rebuild is different: if it fails, it warns and KOLONİ is updated all the same. At the end it says "Restart KOLONİ; the database is migrated when it starts", and where the backup is. -DryRun (Windows) or --dry-run prints the steps without running them.

For Docker, see Install.

items.title: Changelog
items.text: All notable changes to KOLONİ are listed here, newest first. English only.

items.title: Changed
items.text:
• Chat: the Orchestrator no longer stops at a fixed count of steps; it stops when its work is done, when it goes round in circles (it is told once to try another way; then a card asks you Go on or Stop here, tells you on the desktop and at the project's notification address, and ends the turn with its work kept if nobody answers in 10 minutes), or at a limit you set on the Lead role or a trigger. Steps an agent may take now holds sub-agents (docs).
  • To-do, Triggers: in a run nobody watches, an Orchestrator going round in circles ends with the reason on record, and a night or the To-do run goes on with the next job or task; such a turn ends once nothing has moved for Stuck after this many minutes with no progress (Settings › The app, 30 unless you change it), and a To-do task's turn or a night's job after An unattended turn runs at most (hours) (8; empty: no limit) - a night's job no longer stops at 60 minutes (docs).

items.title: Fixed
items.text: • Ready: a team whose coordinator KOLONİ stopped while one of its agents was still at work keeps running until that agent is back, and its work is offered at Ready for you; Ready for you is also asked before the Orchestrator ends its turn where nobody asked it earlier.

  • CLIs: Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot CLI, Qoder and agy on your own plans, signed in by you in your own terminal (docs).

  • CLIs: several Claude Code or Codex accounts side by side, each with its own sign-in for KOLONİ (docs).

  • Workspace: Changes groups every change by what it needs from you, with Approve, Reject and Revert (docs).

  • Knowledge: Add KOLONİ’s own guide makes this guide a knowledge your roles can be given (docs).
  • Knowledge: after a turn, Add to Project notes? keeps fixed findings and docs changes in a Project notes knowledge (docs).
  • Tools: built-in tools by group (files, commands, web, a browser on the sites you allow, team, To-do, memory), given to each role on its Tools tab; five can be switched off for every agent (docs).

  • Install: Python 3.12 to 3.14 on Windows (tested daily) and Linux (automatic tests, less daily use); macOS not tested yet; a Docker image, the newest and least tested (docs).

  • Docs: a user guide in English, published on GitHub Pages and, after one build with the optional Zensical package, served by KOLONİ itself at /guide/, offline and matching the version you run; hints link to it with Learn more → (docs).

items.title: Security
items.text:
• Install: KOLONİ listens on 127.0.0.1 only and sends no telemetry; every request to its API needs the page key, so a plain or injected command an agent runs cannot approve its own cards (docs).
  • Install: exports and backups are downloaded without the page key in their address, so it stays out of your browser's history.
  • Settings: an export without keys also leaves out secret files you attached to a chat (a .env, a key file); the chat keeps their name (docs).
  • Install: a link with a wrong key, from a web page or an agent's answer, no longer locks the page out: the page keeps its key unless KOLONİ accepts the new one, and links in agents' answers and diagrams open in a new tab.
  • Ready: reading secret files, writing most files that steer agents, and commands that delete or send data off the machine stop at a card at every level, with a few exceptions for CLIs run with their own tools (limits); at Full auto these checks are for honest commands, not a wall (docs).
  • Ready: a command an agent runs is judged together with the folder it runs in, so a relative path inside .claude or another protected folder stops at a card as if it were named; Claude Code and Qoder don't say where their shell stands, so their commands are judged at the project root (a cd into a protected folder is itself a card).
  • Ready: KOLONİ's own cards have fixed titles and say KOLONİ asks; an agent's question says The agent asks, so it cannot pass for one of KOLONİ's.
  • Workspace: sub-agents work in working copies, not in your folder, until you take their work in.
  • Agents: your home folder and a drive's root cannot be a project, and KOLONİ's own folder is never opened, even inside a project; a CLI's own Grep and Glob cannot search it either (docs).
  • Agents: web pages, search results, MCP results, knowledge, a GitHub issue and a learned repository's code reach agents framed as data, not instructions; the frame tells the model, it is not a wall; text that tries to give orders shows a Text tried to give orders card (docs).
  • Settings: secret files open only on your Allow once and searches skip them (at Full auto a command that doesn't name the file can still read it); keys in command output show as ***; variables with secret names are kept from commands and CLIs unless you name them (docs).
  • Settings: a planted test key stops a command, web request, browser or MCP call that would send it out.
  • Chat: an agent asks for a key on a Give a secret to its commands? card; the value never reaches the model or the record, and never leaves on a branch (docs).
  • Triggers: turns nobody watches may do only what the trigger allows, and never start a CLI that works with its own tools (docs).
  • Tools: commands can run in a fresh Docker container, with the network off unless you allow it (docs).
  • Tools: MCP servers get only their own variables and what programs need to run, none of KOLONİ's or a CLI's sign-in; one you have not trusted asks before every call (docs).
  • Tools: web searches and requests reach only public addresses; the agents' browser opens only previews and the sites you allow.
  • CLIs: on Windows, a CLI and everything it starts run in a Windows job that is ended on Stop or when KOLONİ closes.
  • Docs: the guide at /guide/ loads its scripts, styles, fonts and pictures only from KOLONİ itself.
  • Docs: report a security problem privately through GitHub's Security tab (docs).

items.title: Knowledge and experts
items.text: Knowledge is "what agents can look things up in": documentation, files or a topic that KOLONİ reads once and turns into a short guide. A role uses a knowledge only if you give it to the role. Open Knowledge on the left rail.

items.title: The Knowledge page
items.text:
Each knowledge is a card. Its header shows its first source, and buttons to Try it and to Learn (later Learn more or Learn again), with what learning may cost beside it. The card also says when it was last read (Fresh:), how much it spent (Spent:), which model it learns with (Learns with:) and which roles use it (Used by:).

The Knowledge page, with this project's code and KOLONİ's own guide offered below the cards.

Click the topic to open the card. Its tabs are Guide, Pages, Not known yet, Settings and Copy.

items.title: Adding knowledge
items.text:
Press + Add knowledge. Pick what it is:

Kind What it reads A docs site A web address. Only the pages under the path you give are read. Files here A folder or a file in this project. A repository A public GitHub repository's address: its code and its docs (below). A folder on this machine A folder outside this project, by its full path, read as a repository is (below). Research a topic A topic to research on the web.

Then:

  • Topic: its name, at most 40 characters. "How agents and the canvas name it."
  • The sources, one a line, at most 10.
  • Learn again weekly (web sources only).
  • Agents may search the web when it has no answer.
  • At most this much a learning (USD): 0.5 unless you change it. It holds only where the model's price is known. On a CLI or a plan the price is not known, so the caps below are what bound a learning.
  • Learn with: the model that writes the guide. By default, the model of a role that uses it. If no role uses it and you pick no model, learning stops and says to choose one.
  • Under More: At most this many pages (a safety cap), 500 unless you change it. For a repository or a folder on this machine, also At most this many code files a learning, 100 unless you change it; 0 writes no guide to its code.

Press Add and learn, or Add without learning to learn later.

items.title: What learning does
items.text:
KOLONİ reads every page under the sources, up to the page cap, and keeps their text in the project's .koloni/knowledge/ folder. A model then writes a guide: what the subject offers, ready functions, short examples and pitfalls, each marked as official, from a single source, or unsure.

The pages read are other people's documents, so KOLONİ keeps them out of the project's git. The guide itself is kept in the folder.

Web pages are read only from public addresses, following the site's robots.txt, and never from another site the page redirects to. Reading stops after 10 minutes.

Learning again reads only what changed. If nothing changed, no model is asked.

This project's code has its own card. "Free: KOLONİ reads the files here, no model." Press Scan the code.

Try it asks a question as an agent would, and shows the answer.

items.title: A repository
items.text:
A repository is learned from three things:

  • Its docs: its README and its other Markdown files, read for a guide as any source's pages are.
  • How the code works: a second part of the guide, written by the model from its code files, the most central first: where a program starts (main, cli, app, index, __init__…), then the files most imported by others. Tests, vendored code and examples are left out. It says what the project does, its main flow, its modules, its key types and functions, and where to start reading.
  • A code map, free: KOLONİ scans its Python, JavaScript and TypeScript files with no model, so agents can ask where a name is defined and who calls it, as for This project's code. The code guide is written from these files too.

On Learn, KOLONİ clones the repository into a temporary folder outside your project, and deletes that folder once it has read it. Only its last commit on its default branch is fetched, over https only, with no tags, submodules or Git LFS files. Nothing of it is run: no hooks, filters or settings of the repository's, and none of your own git settings or credentials. Its files are counted before they are written out: a repository of more than 50,000 files or 300 MB is refused, and so is a clone where less than 2 GB is free (more, for a higher size limit). Both limits are yours to change for every project, in Settings › The app › Agents: Knowledge reads at most (files), from 100 to 1,000,000, and (MB), from 1 to 10,240. A learning keeps the limits it started with. Cloning and reading together stop after 10 minutes.

What stays in your project is text, in the knowledge's folder .koloni/knowledge/<topic>/: its guide, its pages, and its code under code/: the code map, and each code file the map read as code/files/<path>.md, line for line. Test runners and builds look for code files, not .md ones, so they do not pick these up unless set to read Markdown. Files under hidden folders (.github/, .claude/ and the like) are not kept. The code map reads at most 4 MB a file and 64 MB in all. Agents read the code there with read_file, at the file and line lookup names; what they read there is marked as data, not instructions.

What the knowledge keeps is kept out of git, Take in, search, the list of changes and triggers. A working copy links to it rather than copying it, so an agent there reads it too.

Each Learn clones the repository again and reads its docs, the code files already in the guide, and then the next ones, up to the code-file cap. Learning stops at that cap, the page cap, the reading time or the money limit, whichever comes first. The card shows N of M code files in the guide, what stopped it, and Learn more while some are left. With nothing new and nothing changed, a Learn asks no model.

Removing a repository's knowledge deletes its code and pages from the folder; its guide stays. So does making it another kind of source. A knowledge cannot be changed while it learns.

Only GitHub repositories, https://github.com/<owner>/<name>, can be added for now.

items.title: A folder on this machine
items.text:
A folder that is not on GitHub, with git or without, is learned as a repository is: its docs, how its code works and a free code map, the same caps and Learn more. Give its full path, as folder: C:\work\mylib. It is its knowledge's only source.

On Learn, KOLONİ first counts the folder where it is, against the same limits as a repository (50,000 files and 300 MB unless you change them in Settings); over one, the learning stops and keeps nothing new. The count goes into no link or junction, no hidden folder (.git, .github, .vscode…) and no dependency, build or cache folder, in any case (node_modules, .venv, venv, __pycache__, build, dist, target, .next, .tox, htmlcov and the test and type-check caches). Files that are in the cloud alone (OneDrive's, not on this disk) are skipped, not downloaded. Then only the files it counted are read: one added after the count waits for the next Learn.

Nothing is copied into your project but the same text a repository leaves, and nothing is ever written into the folder. Nothing in it is run, not even git: its .git folder is not read.

Only you add one, on the Knowledge page: an agent cannot add or change a folder source, and its expert never learns it by itself. A path is refused if it is not a full path, not a folder, a link or a junction, a drive's root, your home folder or a folder holding it, a hidden folder of your home (.ssh, .claude, .config…), its AppData (on a Mac, its Library), a folder named as secrets are (.ssh), this copy of KOLONİ's folder or its runtime/, another KOLONİ's runtime or checkout (one with data/koloni.db), or this project or a folder in it or around it (use This project's code, or Files here, for those). It is checked again at each Learn.

items.title: KOLONİ's own guide
items.text:
Add KOLONİ's own guide adds this guide as a knowledge called KOLONİ guide. Its source is koloni-guide:. KOLONİ reads only the Markdown pages of its own docs/ folder and keeps them in the project, as for any source. Its code, its .env and runtime/ are never read, and agents read only the kept pages, never KOLONİ's folder.

Adding it learns nothing, because learning costs model calls. Press Learn on its card when you want it; the cost stands beside the button, as for any knowledge. An expert in it never learns it by itself. Give it to a role, and a chat can then ask "what does Summarise a long context at do?" and be answered from the guide.

To remove a knowledge, use the link on its Settings tab. "Its guide stays in the folder." A repository's kept code and pages are deleted.

items.title: Giving knowledge to a role
items.text:
On the Agents page, open a role and its Knowledge tab. Switch a knowledge on, then choose:

  • Map: "its guide, read when its work touches it". Any role can use Map.
  • Full: "its whole guide at each step". Only for your own roles that only read. A role is Full in one knowledge of a project: choosing Full for another of the same project turns the first one to Map. A knowledge of another project, or of every project, stays as it is; where a role is Full in both the project's own and one of every project, the project's own is what it is an expert in. If the role's description is still the one Create expert wrote, it then names the new topic; its name stays. Copying a knowledge to a project where the role is already Full gives it Map.

A role with knowledge can look things up in it while it works.

items.title: Experts
items.text:
An expert is a role that knows one topic and only advises. To make one: Agents → New role → An expert. Fill in Knows (the topic) and its sources, and press Create expert. "It reads its sources once, writes a short guide in the project, and answers from it: it advises and reads only."

The role is named "topic expert". An expert changes nothing: it reads, and answers from its guide. The Orchestrator, or a team's lead, opens it when a job needs it.

When its guide has no answer, an expert with Agents may search the web when it has no answer on may search the web. Below Full auto, an expert's search always asks you first. Without that option, it asks you whether to search. After it finds something on the web, a card asks whether to add it to the guide (Add / Not now); it is added the next time the knowledge learns.

items.title: Project notes
items.text:
At the end of a turn, KOLONİ may ask Add to Project notes? It lists findings that were fixed and changes to the project's docs/, at most 8. Tick the ones to keep and press Add, or Not now.

What you add goes into a knowledge called Project notes, made the first time you add. KOLONİ writes its guide itself, with no model.

Project notes and Knowledge are not the project's Memory.

items.title: Memory
items.text:
Memory is what a project remembers between chats: your preferences, the project's rules, facts you approved, and notes agents wrote while they worked. Open it with Memory on the left rail. Each project has its own memory.

KOLONİ never shows a memory as surer than it is. A fact rests on lines of a file, and KOLONİ checks those lines again each time it reads the fact.

From a note to an approved fact, and how agents get it.

items.title: The kinds of memory
items.text:
Kind Who writes it Where you see it Your preferences You. One text, used in every project. Told tab This project's rules You. Kept in the folder's .koloni/rules.md, so they go into git with the project. Told tab Facts (the core) You, or an agent's proposal that you approved. Facts tab Notes (the journal) Agents, while they work, and KOLONİ's own note-taker if you switch it on. Notes tab

A fact has a subject (a few words, such as test command) and usually a source: a file and a range of lines. The core holds at most 4 000 characters of facts; the Facts tab shows how much is used.

KOLONİ may also suggest a preference. It shows under Your preferences with a "suggested" tag and the buttons Add and Reject.

items.title: The three ways memory reaches an agent
items.text:
The page has four tabs. The first three are the three ways memory reaches an agent:

  1. Told: "Said to every agent, always." Your preferences and the project's rules are put in every agent's briefing.
  2. Facts: "Given to an agent when its work names the subject." When every word of a fact's subject appears in the agent's task, the fact is given to it. The agent is also told how many other facts exist, so it can look them up. A fact whose subject is too general to match is only found by looking it up.
  3. Notes: "Found only when an agent looks." Notes are never given by themselves. An agent finds them with its Recall tool ("look in memory").

The fourth tab, History, shows decisions and what was removed.

While an agent works, KOLONİ keeps checking what it was given. If a fact it was given changes or is removed during its work, the agent is told.

In an agent's window, under Details › Every step as recorded, you can see what that agent got: Given from memory and Looked up in memory.

items.title: Sources and evidence
items.text:
Most facts and notes point to a file and its lines. KOLONİ keeps a fingerprint of those lines and compares it each time memory is read. Next to each one you see what it found:

What you see What it means source unchanged since noted The lines read exactly as they did when the record was written. source moved since noted: check again The same lines are now somewhere else in the file. source changed since noted: check again The lines are different now, or gone. no source The record does not point to a file.

"Source unchanged" only means the file lines read as they did. It does not mean the record is right.

A fact whose source changed or moved is given to no agent until you look at it again. Open it with Look again. You see the lines as they read now, and you can choose:

  • These are the same lines (only when they moved): the fact now points to the new place.
  • Correct: rewrite the fact.
  • Remove: take it out of the core.

Look at the sources again, at the top of the page, checks every source again.

A record written in a turn nobody watched (a trigger's turn) is tagged "written with nobody watching".

items.title: Who writes what
items.text:
Agents write notes. An agent with the Remember tool ("note what it found") adds a note to the journal. A few rules apply:

  • A note about a file must name the lines, and the agent must have read those lines in this turn.
  • Text that reads like an instruction is refused.
  • A newer note on the same subject replaces the older one.

Agents propose facts; you approve them. An agent can put a note forward for the core. Nothing enters the core unless you approve it. Waiting proposals show above the tabs, with a line such as "1 fact waits for your word". For each one you can choose Approve, Edit and approve (then Approve as edited) or Reject. If it would replace a fact on the same subject, you see both side by side.

A proposal can be approved only while its source is unchanged, and not if the file was changed in the same turn the note was written. A note on a subject the core already has a fact on waits for you too; until you decide, no agent is given it and Recall does not find it.

You write facts yourself. On the Facts tab, ＋ Add a fact asks for the fact, its subject and, if you like, a file with its first and last line. Add to the core saves it. It replaces any fact on the same subject. A fact's ⋯ menu has Correct and Remove. A note's ⋯ menu has Remove and Make it a fact.

Your words on a card become a fact. When you ask for changes on a card and say why, that text is kept as a fact, shown as "said by you at a card, asking for changes".

Preferences and rules are yours alone. No agent writes them.

Automatic notes are off by default. Switch them on under Settings › This project › Memory and web › Note what the work found, by itself. After each message's work, a fast model writes at most three notes of what it found. That is one more model request after every message, on your plan or your bill. These notes go into the journal, signed as that model's. They never go into the core by themselves and never replace an agent's note or a fact.

In a turn nobody watches, agents can still write notes, but nothing is put forward for the core.

items.title: Searching memory
items.text:
One search box sits above the tabs: "Search everything this project remembers".

  • Typing filters what is on the page. Every word must match.
  • Search deeper (or Enter) runs the same search an agent's Recall does. It looks in the project's memory, in earlier messages, and in the memory of linked projects. Results are grouped under "In earlier messages" and "In linked projects".

Search deeper finds the word in earlier messages, with who said it and when.

Earlier messages means your messages, the Orchestrator's last answers, sub-agents' reports and closed To-do tasks. Tool output is not searched.

You can also start a deep search from Ctrl+K with Search in messages.

Search by words or by meaning. The by words ▾ button opens "Search by meaning with". Pick a provider that has a server address, and an embedding model (text-embedding-3-small unless you change it). Search then also finds records that mean the same thing in other words, tagged "by meaning". With off: by words alone, only words are matched. If the provider fails, the results say that search by meaning is off, and why.

Search by meaning costs one embeddings request to that provider for each search, on your plan or your bill. That request also carries up to 50 notes, facts or earlier messages that were not read yet. Nothing is sent when a note or fact is written.

Memory of other projects. Under Settings › This project › Memory and web › Also look in the memory of, tick other projects. Their records are found by Search deeper and Recall, but never given to an agent at its start.

items.title: Project notes and Knowledge are not memory
items.text:
• Knowledge (its own page on the rail) holds expert topics learned from web pages or project files. Roles use them while they work. See Knowledge and experts.
  • Project notes is a Knowledge topic that KOLONİ fills from what you tick on the Add to Project notes? card at the end of a turn.

Neither is on the Memory page. Memory is short facts and notes, each checked against its source. Knowledge is longer material an expert reads.

items.title: History and Export
items.text:
The History tab says "Decisions and what was removed. Nothing is deleted."

  • Recent decisions lists the latest decisions, such as "Approved into the core", "Corrected", "Rejected" or "Removed".
  • Removed / replaced lists what was removed or replaced. Any of these can be brought back with Take back.

Correcting a fact keeps the old one as replaced. Removing or rejecting never deletes a record.

Export, at the top of the page, downloads the core as MEMORY.md: each fact with its subject, who wrote it and when, and its source with its status now. Only facts are exported, not notes. The file is a copy to read; editing it does not change the memory.

To take everything KOLONİ keeps, memory included, use Export everything under Settings › The app › Your data. See Settings.

items.title: FAQ
items.text:
Why didn't an agent use a fact I approved? A fact is given only when the agent's task names every word of its subject, and only while its source is unchanged. Check the fact's status on the Facts tab. The agent can still find it with Recall.

A fact says "source changed". Is it wrong now? Not necessarily. Its lines changed, so KOLONİ stopped giving it to agents until you look. Open Look again and correct, confirm or remove it.

Can an agent change the core without me? No. Agents write notes and proposals. Only your approval, or your own words, put a fact in the core.

How do I make agents always follow something? Write it in This project's rules (for this project) or Your preferences (for every project). Both are told to every agent.

Does memory leave my machine? Memory is given to the models your agents run on, as part of their work. Search by meaning sends text to the provider you picked for it.

Can I delete a memory for good? Not from the page. Removing hides it from agents and keeps it in History, where you can take it back.

items.text: What is planned after 0.1.0. Plans change; nothing here is promised.

items.title: Planned for 0.2.0

  • Add a GitHub issue to the To-do (a chat can already start from one).
  • Pull requests outside GitHub, such as GitLab.
  • Who wrote this line: the agent and the turn behind each change.
  • Codex and Copilot sessions that carry on across turns, and support for Copilot Fusion, a model choice in GitHub Copilot CLI.
  • Voice: your own speech server, hands-free spoken conversation, and a voice for each role.
  • Models that make images, audio and video, on the canvas and for roles.
  • Remote MCP servers (reached over HTTP, with sign-in).
  • Plugins that install a package's parts into KOLONİ.
  • Arranging agents on the canvas: tools to group and place them.
  • Screen control: only apps you pick, each action or session asked, never in a turn nobody watches. This needs a design first.

  • New screenshots and videos in this guide.

items.title: Settings
items.text: The Settings page holds everything you set for one chat, for one project and for KOLONİ as a whole.

items.title: Opening Settings
items.text:
• Press Settings (the gear) at the bottom of the left rail. It opens on This project, or on The app for a chat with no folder. Press it again, or the close button, to close the page.
  • Or press Ctrl+K and choose Settings. Ctrl+K also lists each section by name (the app's with "(the app)" after it), and opens Settings right at it.
  • Under the message box, Chat (the gear at the end of the model's line; under More in a narrow chat) opens this chat's short sheet; its All settings opens Settings at This chat.

Choosing another page on the rail closes Settings. The chat under it stays as it was, so a message you were typing is kept.

items.title: Three levels
items.text:
The levels are listed on the left, always in this order, each with its sections under it:

Level What it covers This chat The open chat's own settings. Shown while a chat is open. This project The project of the open chat. Shown only when the chat has a folder. Every chat of the project follows it, the ones made before too. The app The whole app, in every project. Always there.

A chat takes what it does not set from its project, and the project from the app. Each setting is set at one level only: This chat shows what it takes from the project, read only, with a link up. What you type at one level is kept while you look at another.

items.title: Saving
items.text:
Each section has its own Save button. It is on only when something changed and every value is valid. After saving, the button says "Saved".

A section with changes you have not saved shows a not saved tag next to its name in the list. You can move between sections without losing those changes. Three sections have no Save button for the whole section and save each row on its own: Runs without asking, Slash commands and This folder. This chat's settings take effect as you change them.

items.title: This chat
items.text:
The same rows as the sheet under Chat under the message box:

Setting What it does Teams Who picks this chat's teams, and the ones picked. Set with the Teams button over the canvas. Folders Where this chat's agents work, and its other folders. Set with the folder button. Page scripts Ask each time or Always run in this chat, for a page an agent shows in the Workspace. Also offered over the page's preview. Runs without asking A project's chat: how many rules it has, and a link to This project › Runs without asking. A chat with no folder keeps its own list here.

Its permission level, Plan first and its model stay under the message box. Under them, From the project lists what the chat takes from its project (who changes the files, opening a sub-agent, when you're away, the agents' limits, money, where commands run) with Change in This project, and Change in The app leads to the app's. A chat with no folder says that its sub-agents use KOLONİ's defaults: ask when it matters, 2 at the same time, 2 levels, 6 per request.

items.title: This project
items.text:
The sections are listed on the left, in this order.

Settings › This project, at its first section, Agents.

items.title: Agents
items.text:
"Every chat of this project follows these, the ones made before too."

Setting What it does Who changes the files Orchestrator delegates the work: it plans, asks and checks; sub-agents change the files. Orchestrator decides: a small change (one or two files, a few lines) it makes itself, bigger work goes to a sub-agent. Orchestrator does it itself: it changes the files itself, and may still hand a part to a sub-agent. Finish only when the tests pass An agent on Claude Code that changed files is sent back to work, at most twice, while the tests fail. KOLONİ runs the tests where this project's commands run, by itself only in Full auto or under an Always run rule. Have a model look over each sub-agent's report The Observer role's model reads each sub-agent's report, the diffs and the test output, and says what the record shows. One more model request per report. The Orchestrator takes its words as an opinion, not a fact. Suggest follow-up tasks after each turn On by default. After a turn that did something, the Assistant PO proposes at most three follow-up tasks for the To-do list; they wait for your Add, Edit or Reject. One small model request per such turn, made once the turn is over, and at Full auto in a turn you started one more for the Orchestrator's decision. Follow-up tasks from picks the tier: Fast tier (the default), Balanced tier or Strongest tier.

items.title: Asking and away
items.text: Setting What it does Opening a sub-agent Ask when it matters, Always ask or Never ask. With Never ask, sub-agents open on their own in every chat of this project. When you're away Everything waits for you, or The Orchestrator answers what it safely can, after a number of minutes (0 to 1440). With the second, once you haven't answered for that long (or the away card is on), the Orchestrator picks, says why, and you see it under "Decided for you". It opens a sub-agent on its role's own model unless that model is at its limit, out of credit, or over this month's budget; a move onto another model that may cost money, commands it may not run, deleting, reaching outside and Take in still wait. An Orchestrator on a CLI uses one request of your plan for each answer.

items.title: New chats start with
items.text:
"A new chat of this project starts with these; each chat then sets its own."

Setting What it does New chats' teams Orchestrator decides, Manual or No teams. With Manual, the teams a chat kept with Use for new chats in this project. Other folders The folders a new chat starts with, besides the project. Remove one here; add one from a chat's folder button with Keep for this project.

A room's limits: "What a room opened in any chat of this project may spend, unless you say otherwise as you open it. Empty: no limit." This is their one place: Work together… sets a room's own.

Setting What it does Posts, at most 1 to 1000. Minutes, at most 1 to 1440. Tokens, at most A token budget for the room. Tokens, at least 60,000 by default. A room an agent opens with a smaller token budget gets this many, because one member's step takes about 8,000 to 9,000 tokens. If it is higher than Tokens, at most, the room gets the most. Empty: an agent's room gets what it asks for.

items.title: Limits and money
items.text: Setting What it does At most this many agents at work in this project Counted over all of this project's chats together. A new agent waits for a free place. Empty: no limit. Agents at the same time The most agents at work at once for one message. 1 to 32. Each provider has its own limit too. Above 8 the page warns that this may strain this machine and your subscription. Sub-agent levels How deep sub-agents may open their own, from 1 to 4. Sub-agents per request The most sub-agents opened for one message outside a recipe. 1 to 20. Continue gives this many more steps How many more steps Continue gives an agent that stopped at a step limit, on its card or on its kept work's card. 25 unless you change it, 1 to 200. A go on by message gives a new step limit instead. The step limit itself is the app's: Steps an agent may take, a link away. See Step limits. Stop the work on a message over this many tokens Empty: no limit. A discussion's tokens, at most A token budget for each discussion. Empty: no limit. See Discussions. Monthly budget For this calendar month's messages, in the currency of your prices (else USD). At 80% you are told. At 100% a new message asks before its work starts, and triggers start none. Work on a model with no price is not counted.

items.title: Commands and secrets
items.text:
Heading: "Run commands on".

Setting What it does This machine Commands use the project's own tools as they are. They are not isolated. The page also says which shell commands run in. Docker container A fresh container for each command, with this folder mounted. Only the folder is kept. Needs Docker running. Then: Image (for example python:3.12, never pulled for you) and Allow network access. On Linux and macOS a command runs as your user, not as root, so the files it makes are yours, except under rootless Docker. Hide secret files from commands On by default. Covers commands in Docker and in Copilot's sandbox. Secret variables commands may see Environment variables with secret names are held back from commands and CLIs. Name the ones they may see, separated by commas, for example OPENAI_API_KEY, NPM_TOKEN. The page lists what is held back. Copilot's commands never get GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN or COPILOT_*, whatever you name here: it signs in its own way. Planted test key (canary) On by default. Each message's commands get a made-up key that no agent is told of. A command, web request, browser or MCP call that would send it out is refused and the work stops: something the agent read may have told it to.

items.title: Runs without asking
items.text:
• Sites agents open: the agents' own browsers open these in every chat of this project without asking, unless marked Ask first. Add one with Allow site.
  • Commands and requests, by chat: the rules made with Always run on a card, grouped by chat. Remove one with its ✕. You can also allow plain GET requests to a host for a chat.

See Permission levels for what a rule can and cannot cover.

items.title: Checks and git
items.text:
Heading: "When a sub-agent's work is added".

Setting What it does Test before adding A command run on a sub-agent's changes in its working copy, for example python -m pytest -q. Only an exit code of 0 passes. Empty: no test. Measure command A command whose last line of output is a score from 0 to 100, for example python measure.py. Recipes use it to pick the best of several candidates. Save each sub-agent's work as a git commit One commit per piece of work, offered on the card once the changes are in, and only where this folder is the top of a git repository. It is always your click, never made by itself, and nothing is pushed. How a team's finished branch reaches yours Merge here or Open a pull request. If you have not chosen, the first finished branch on a GitHub project asks.

items.title: Memory and web
items.text: Setting What it does Note what the work found, by itself After each message's work, a fast model writes at most three notes of what it found. One more model request after every message. Off by default. See Memory. Search by meaning with The provider whose server embeds the memory for the search by meaning, and its Embedding model; off, the search goes by words alone. One embeddings request for each search. The Memory page sets it too. Also look in the memory of Tick other projects. Agents' look-ups and your deep search find their memory too. Search address (SearXNG) Your own SearXNG server, for example http://localhost:8888. An agent's web search asks it first; turn on its JSON format. When it does not answer, the search goes on as below and says so. Otherwise search with The built-in search first, then a CLI or A CLI first, then the built-in search. Let agy search too Lets agy search the web. While it searches, agy is not held to its search tool: it may read files on this machine or open pages unasked.

items.title: Notifications
items.text: Setting What it does Notification address A webhook address KOLONİ posts to. Once set, it is not shown again; type a new one to replace it. Post it as JSON {"text": …} (Slack, Mattermost), JSON {"content": …} (Discord) or Plain text (ntfy). Show a desktop notification Windows only. Remove the notification address Shown when an address is set. Send the day's summary at A time of day, by this computer's clock, for a daily summary: the Board's Today numbers as text, counted from the record; no model is asked. Needs an address or desktop notifications. If KOLONİ is closed then, it sends the summary late, when it next opens, and only for the last day it missed.

items.title: Slash commands
items.text: Your own commands for the message box. Each has a Name, What it does, the Text it puts in the box, and can Hand it to a role. Tick In every project to use it everywhere. Add command saves a new one; Edit and Delete change the list.

items.title: This folder
items.text:
Project map is a table of the project's parts: Folder, Language, Files, AGENTS.md and Test command. You can change a part's test command and save that row; Use guess puts back the one KOLONİ found.

This folder's rules are shown when the folder has .koloni/rules.md. Read-only here; you change the rules on the Memory page.

items.title: Delete project
items.text:
Under This folder, Delete project… removes the project from KOLONİ: its chats with their messages, agents' work and usage, its memory, knowledge, To-do tasks, triggers and work while you're away. The dialog counts what goes, offers Export first (the same .zip as Export everything, without API keys), and deletes only once you type the project's name. It cannot be undone.

The folder on disk is not touched: its files, its git and its .koloni/ stay. Opening the folder again makes it a new, empty project. What KOLONİ kept of its chats under runtime/ goes, as a chat's delete takes it: their attachments and their CLI sessions.

While anything of the project is at work (a turn, a sub-agent, a room, a trigger's or the To-do's turn, jobs while you're away), while a command it started still runs (such as a dev server), while finished work waits for Take in or Discard, or while its knowledge is learning, the delete is refused and says why.

items.title: Agents, in every project
items.text: Setting What it does Answer in The language the agents write in, in every project. Auto means the language you write in. Pick one from the list (English, Türkçe, Deutsch, Español, Français, Italiano, Português) or type another. KOLONİ's own screens stay in English. Steps an agent may take The most model steps one sub-agent takes on a job before it stops: 25 unless you change it, a whole number from 5 to 200. Coordinators get more for their recipes. The Orchestrator counts no steps: it stops when it goes round in circles, or at its role's own limit if you set one. What Continue gives on top is each project's: This project › Limits and money, a link away. What happens at the limit, and who may give more: Step limits. Stuck after this many minutes with no progress In work nobody watches - a To-do task, a job while you're away, a trigger's run (only where its Minutes a run are longer) - the Orchestrator's turn ends once nothing has moved for this long: no file of the turn changed, no agent finished its work, no failing command passed. Each of those starts the minutes again; a card waiting for you, a command or a model step under way, or an agent below the Orchestrator at work keeps them from running out. 30 unless you change it, a whole number from 5 to 1,440. The turn fails with the reason, its work kept; a To-do task gets its fix round, then is blocked, and the run goes on. See Step limits. An unattended turn runs at most (hours) A last resort: a To-do task's turn or a job while you're away ends after this many hours however it goes, its work kept. 8 unless you change it, a whole number from 1 to 72; empty: no limit, so a turn that keeps working (changes, agents at work, messages between agents) can run without end. A trigger's own Minutes a run holds its runs. Summarise a long context at (%) Once an agent's context passes this much of its model's window, the older part is summarised before its next step. A whole number from 50 to 95. It does not apply to a CLI run step by step, nor to Claude Code run natively with its own sign-in for KOLONİ, which compacts its own session. Any other CLI starts each turn anew: KOLONİ compacts it, against its role's window. See Set up a CLI. Knowledge reads at most (files) Knowledge from a repository or a folder on this machine stops before it reads more files than this: 50,000 unless you change it, a whole number from 100 to 1,000,000. A learning keeps what it started with. See Knowledge. Knowledge reads at most (MB) The same, in MB: 300 unless you change it, from 1 to 10,240.

items.title: Voice
items.text: This browser's, for every chat: Auto-read reads (the whole answer or a short summary), the Dictation language, Read aloud with the browser's own voice (its Rate and Pitch) or Read aloud with Gemini (a Gemini API key, and How Gemini says it), and How the Orchestrator speaks. Dictate and Read aloud stay beside the message box. See Voice.

items.title: Your data
items.text:
Export: your KOLONİ data in one .zip: chats, agents, providers, memory, triggers, skills and attachments. Not in it: your project folders (their .koloni/ knowledge too), working copies, logs, previews, the CLIs' own folders and the database's upgrade backups.

  • Include API keys and secrets (keep this file safe): without this, the keys KOLONİ stores in its settings and secret files you attached to a chat (a .env, a key file) are left out. A key that was ever written in a chat, in another file you attached, an agent's output or a command stays in the file either way, so keep the file private.
  • Export everything starts the download.

Restore: "Restore only a file you exported yourself: it decides which programs KOLONİ may start."

  • Restore from a file… takes a .zip you exported.
  • Nothing changes at once. The restore replaces your data the next time KOLONİ starts: close KOLONİ and start it again. Until then you can Cancel it. Your data as it was is set aside, not deleted.
  • After a restore, triggers and to-do work wait until you press Resume.
  • If the file had no keys, the page lists the providers that need theirs again.

Under them: how much space KOLONİ's database, backups, working copies and logs take, and Always blocked, the places no agent ever opens, in every project; the list is KOLONİ's own and cannot be changed here.

items.title: Settings kept in the folder
items.text:
A few project settings are also written to the folder's .koloni/settings.json, so they travel with the project in git: where commands run (this machine or Docker), the Docker image, Docker's network access, and the web search order. The first time, the page says "Saved in .koloni/ in this folder (kept in git)". Secrets, your addresses and this machine's folders stay in KOLONİ only. Everything under The app stays in KOLONİ too.

When a folder's settings differ from KOLONİ's (for example, after a git pull from another machine), the top of This project asks whether to use them, with Use them and Not now.

items.title: Troubleshooting and FAQ
items.text: The messages below are the ones KOLONİ shows, word for word. Text in {braces} is filled in by KOLONİ.

items.title: Starting and opening
items.text: "Open KOLONİ from the link in its window" ("Each start of KOLONİ makes a new link.") You opened an old tab or a bookmark after KOLONİ restarted. Each start makes a new page key. Copy the link KOLONİ printed in its window (KOLONİ is open at http://127.0.0.1:8790/#key=…) and paste it there. "KOLONİ cannot reach its server" The page cannot reach KOLONİ. Check that KOLONİ still runs in its window, then press Try again. "This page could not be shown" "Often the page and the server are different versions: restart KOLONİ, then reload. The other pages still work." This often happens right after an update. Restart KOLONİ, then press Reload. "KOLONİ serves your keys and files with no TLS: bind to this machine (KOLONI_HOST=… is not), or run the image." KOLONİ stopped because KOLONI_HOST names an address other than this machine. Use 127.0.0.1 (the default), ::1 or localhost, or run the Docker image. The port is already in use KOLONİ has no message of its own for this; the error comes from the system. Another KOLONİ (or another program) uses port 8790. Start KOLONİ on another port with KOLONI_PORT, and give it its own KOLONI_RUNTIME_ROOT. See Install.

items.title: Updating
items.text:
The update script stops at the first problem and prints update: {why} - stopped, nothing after it ran. The reasons:

{why} What to do tracked files have uncommitted changes: commit or stash them first Commit or stash your own changes to KOLONİ's files, then run it again. something answers on 127.0.0.1:{port} - stop KOLONİ first (Ctrl+C in its window) Stop KOLONİ, then run it again. this folder is not a git checkout; update it with git first (git clone) KOLONİ's folder must be a git checkout. this is a linked working copy; run the update in the main checkout Run the script in the main KOLONİ folder. {step} failed That step's own output says why.

When it works, it says Updated to {commit}. Restart KOLONİ; the database is migrated when it starts, and where the backup is.

items.title: Models
items.text: "{Provider} isn't answering at {address}." The bar at the top. The model server does not answer. Start it (for a server on this machine, Models → the provider → Server), or press Pick another model. The bar speaks only of the providers the open chat would run on: the one chosen for the chat, and where its Orchestrator and roles would run. With several down it names them all ("2 providers aren't answering: …"); Details lists each. ✕ hides it for this session until something else goes wrong. "{Role} can't run: {why}" The bar at the top. A role this chat would use (the Orchestrator, too) cannot run where it would now: its model is not one its provider may run, or the provider cannot be opened here. Pick another model for the role on the Agents page, or change the provider's list on the Models page. "{Provider} has no model it may run with by default." The provider's default model is not one it may run. Open the provider on the Models page and check its Default model. "{model} does not support tool calls; chat works, file tools are off." This model can talk but cannot use KOLONİ's tools. Pick a model that supports tool calls. For llama.cpp, start llama-server with --jinja. "The {command} command was not found on this machine. Install it in your own terminal (KOLONİ does not), then press Check on the Models tab" The CLI is not installed, or not on your PATH. Install it with the command shown, or set Path to the command on the provider's Connection tab. The card says "not installed". "{command} is not signed in. Sign in in your own terminal (KOLONİ does not), then press Check on the Models tab" Sign in to the CLI in your own terminal with the command shown, then press Check. The card says "not signed in". "The {command} command was found. It was not run, so sign-in is not checked." This is what Test says for a CLI. To check sign-in too, press Try a real run. It counts against your plan. "Qoder: in the model's queue for {time} (waits up to {time})" In the agent's window; its box on the canvas says "queued {time}". Qoder holds a free model's request in a queue while the model is busy. In tests the wait was about 1 to 3 minutes. Wait, or pick another model for the chat or the role. A sub-agent whose model KOLONİ picked by tier is moved to the tier's next model after 90 seconds, if the tier has another. See Qoder's free models. "Copilot can't use {model} on your account: pick another model" Or, when Copilot runs as a session: "GitHub Copilot CLI exited with code 1: Error: Model "{model}" from --model flag is not available." KOLONİ's list offers a model that your Copilot account or CLI does not. Pick another model. So that agents do not pick it by its tier, switch the model's On off on the Copilot provider's Models tab. "{CLI} {version} could not be asked before it acts ({why}); run it as a session instead" Seen with Qoder run Native, with the reason "it did not apply KOLONİ's hook". KOLONİ runs a CLI with its own tools only when the CLI asks KOLONİ before each tool, and this one did not, so nothing ran. Open the provider and set How it runs to One session per agent, with KOLONİ's tools. See Set up a CLI. Tokens show as "–" or "unknown" for a CLI GitHub Copilot CLI run as a session reports no token counts, and KOLONİ estimates none. The Usage page shows "–" and the agent's window "unknown". Run Native, it reports its tokens and AI credits (or premium requests). A CLI on a plan never has a cost either. To see how much of your plan is used, look at the provider's plan meter, which Copilot has on your GitHub account (not on a model server of your own). See Usage and budgets.

items.title: When a turn fails
items.text:
A failed turn shows "Run failed: {Provider}: {reason}." with a next step under it:

Reason Next step shown limit reached, resets "Wait until it resets, or pick another model." out of credits "Add credits to that account, or pick another model." not signed in, or its key was refused "Sign in to it again, or pick another model." the CLI stopped without finishing "Send the message again." it ended without an answer "Send the message again." model server unreachable "Check that the model server is running, or pick another model." no model provider is set up "Add one on the Models page." "the CLI stopped without finishing" The CLI closed in the middle of its turn. The turn ends within a few seconds, even if a command the CLI started was still running. The programs it started end with it, as they do when you press Stop, so none keeps running or spending your plan. "model server did not start answering within {seconds} seconds" The model took too long to start. A large local model can be slow to load. Raise KOLONI_MODEL_FIRST_TOKEN_SECONDS (default 900) before you start KOLONİ. "model server sent nothing for {seconds} seconds" The model stopped in the middle of an answer. Raise KOLONI_MODEL_STALL_SECONDS (default 120) if your model pauses for long. "Interrupted by a server restart. Send a message to continue." KOLONİ stopped while the turn ran. Nothing is run again by itself. Send a message to go on. "Stopped at its step limit." An agent used all its steps for this job. A sub-agent's limit is Settings › The app › Agents › Steps an agent may take, with more for a coordinator's recipe. The Orchestrator has none unless you set one on the Lead role. Send a message to go on, or split big work into smaller messages. See Step limits. "stopped going round in circles: …" The Orchestrator repeated a call with the same result 10 times in a row, or the same call failed the same way 5 times, with nothing moving in between. In a turn you started a card asked you first: Go on or Stop here. Read its last calls in the chat, then say in a new message what to do differently. See Step limits. "{name} came to its limit of {taken} steps before its work was done." A sub-agent with nothing kept reached the app's step limit, and its card asks: Continue (+{n} steps) or Stop here. At Full auto the Orchestrator answers it once for each agent in a turn. See Step limits. "stopped at its role's limit of {limit} steps" A sub-agent reached the step limit set on its role. While the turn still runs, its kept work's card offers Continue (+{n} steps); {n} is Settings › This project › Limits and money › Continue gives this many more steps. Without kept work there is no card. Only you give more past a role's limit: the Orchestrator's go on is refused there, at Full auto and while you're away too. The role's limit counts the agent's earlier steps, in later turns too: after the turn, raise At most this many steps under Safety stops for one agent in the role's form (Agents page), then ask the Orchestrator to go on. A CLI working with its own tools takes no steps KOLONİ can count, so this limit does not hold it. "Stopped after the {n} steps it was given" An agent reached the end of the steps it was given by a Continue, or by the Orchestrator's call at Full auto. {n} is the job's whole count, the steps it had taken plus those given: after a Continue of 25 at 25 steps it reads 50. No Continue / Stop here card comes for it again in this turn. If it changed files, its kept work's card has Continue while the turn runs; otherwise ask for more in your next message. See Step limits. "could not work: Codex kept trying its own tools, which are off in step mode. Try running Codex as One session per agent (Models › Codex › How it runs)." Or "could not review: …" for a reviewer. Run as One run per model step, Codex sometimes tries its own tools, which KOLONİ switches off there. KOLONİ tells it to use KOLONİ's tools and tries the step again. A step that asks for any of KOLONİ's tools starts the count anew. The third such step in a row (one that tried Codex's own tools and asked for none of KOLONİ's) ends the agent. Each step tried again counts toward its step limit. Open the Codex provider and set How it runs to One session per agent, Codex's default for a provider added since 7 Nov 2026 (on a model server of your own it starts as One run per model step: its session there is not yet measured, so try it there knowing that): it keeps working with KOLONİ's tools, triggers included. To let Codex use its own tools instead, set it to Native. Triggers never start a Native CLI, so a trigger then no longer runs its turns on Codex (see FAQ). See Set up a CLI. "budget: stopped after {steps} model steps, the most this trigger gives a turn" A trigger's run used its budget. Raise Model steps a run on the trigger. See Triggers.

items.title: Money
items.text: "Over this month's budget. Send it anyway?" The project's monthly budget is used up. Press Go on anyway to send it, or Cancel. A   provider's own limit shows the same way, starting "Over {provider}'s limit of …". Change the budget   under Settings › This project › Limits and money, and a provider's limits on its Limits tab.

items.title: Triggers
items.text: "It would have asked you:" A trigger's turn met something it was not allowed to do. "Each was refused, and nothing was done in   its place." Press Allow this in the trigger to open the trigger's form with it ticked; it is   yours to save. "this project is over this month's budget: nothing was started" and "the provider its Orchestrator runs on is over its limit: nothing was started" A trigger did not start because of a budget or a limit.

items.title: Commands and Docker
items.text:
"Docker is not running: a container cannot be chosen." Settings › This project › Commands and secrets. Start Docker, then open the page again. "the image {image} is not on this machine; run: docker pull {image}" KOLONİ never pulls an image for you. Run the command shown in your own terminal. "Permission denied" on files in the project, with commands in Docker on Linux Commands in Docker run as your user now. Files an older version of KOLONİ made in the project, such as dist/, node_modules/ or .coverage, may still belong to root. Give them back to yourself in your own terminal, in the project's folder: sudo chown -R "$(id -u):$(id -g)" . You rejected a command, and the same change comes back as a file change

You rejected a command that writes a file or applies a patch. The agent is told "If the change is still needed, make it with edit_file / write_file", so it makes the same change as a file change:

  • at Ask before changes, it waits on a file-change card with its diff;
  • at Auto-edit files, it is written at once, and Revert takes it back;
  • from a sub-agent, it comes back with its working copy's card (Take in or Discard).

If you do not want the change at all, tell the agent so. See Permission levels.

items.title: Taking work in
items.text: "Changed on both sides, and git does not put them together: {files}" You and an agent changed the same lines. Press Let an agent resolve the conflicts, or resolve   them yourself. "Your uncommitted changes are in the way (commit, stash or unstage them first): {files}" Commit, stash or unstage your own changes to those files, then try again.

items.title: Folders
items.text: "{path} cannot be opened as a folder: {why}" Some places are never opened as a project: a drive's root, a folder that holds your home folder's secrets (such as .ssh or a CLI's settings), KOLONİ's own folder, and network paths. In the folder browser they are tagged "always blocked". Pick a folder inside your projects instead.

items.title: Restore
items.text: "not restored: {why}" The file could not be restored. For example, "it is not a KOLONİ export: it has no manifest.json", or "it was made by a newer KOLONİ (…): update KOLONİ first". Restore only a file you exported yourself. "A restore could not be applied at the last start: it is kept in {path}, and KOLONİ's log says why." Your data was not replaced. KOLONİ's log, in runtime/logs/koloni.log, says why.

items.title: This guide
items.text: "The guide is not built yet" At /guide/, or after a Learn more → link. KOLONİ serves this guide only once it is built. Run the commands that page shows in KOLONİ's folder, then reload. See This guide inside KOLONİ. On GitHub, the guide is not published Only in your own copy of KOLONİ on GitHub. The Guide workflow builds this guide and pushes it to the gh-pages branch; it publishes by itself only once the repository variable PAGES_ENABLED is true (a run by hand always publishes). The site shows only after Settings → Pages → Deploy from a branch, gh-pages, / (root). A broken link or anchor fails the build, and nothing is published.

items.title: FAQ
items.text:
Is anything on screen simulated? No. The canvas, the agents and the usage come from what was recorded. A value KOLONİ does not know is shown as unknown.

Does KOLONİ send anything about me? No telemetry. What leaves your machine is the requests to the providers you add, and the web searches, requests and tools you allow. See Data and privacy.

Can I give a running command some input? No. Commands cannot be given input while they run.

Why did my trigger not start on a CLI? Triggers do not start a turn on a CLI that works with its own tools (Native, or agy).

Why can an agent still read .env at Full auto? A script that opens .env without naming it (it builds the name, say) is not caught. A command that names it, or searches the whole folder, is asked about at every level, but when it runs Native, Codex runs the reads its own rules count as safe without asking KOLONİ, and agy reading with its own tools reads it without asking at any level. Only Docker and Copilot's sandbox hide secret files from commands. See Known limits and Permission levels.

Are canvas positions saved? No. The canvas is drawn from the record each time.

Which systems are tested? Windows the most. Linux and the Docker image less, macOS not yet. See Install.

items.title: Discussions
items.text: A discussion is several agents talking one question through in rounds, while nobody changes anything.

items.title: Who starts one
items.text:
An agent starts a discussion when it has the discuss tool. You cannot start one yourself, but you can join it.

An agent invites 1 to 5 agents or roles, for 1 to 20 rounds (3 unless it says otherwise). The agent that opened it speaks last in each round.

items.title: When it ends
items.text:
A discussion ends when nobody has anything to add, at its round limit, when it reaches its token budget, or when you end it. It also ends at the message's and the project's own limits.

Each step of a speech sends the speaker's whole work so far again, so the token count grows faster than the talk does. The budget is set under Settings › This project › Limits and money › A discussion's tokens, at most. Empty means no limit. It applies to discussions opened after you save it. A chat with no folder has no token limit for its discussions.

items.title: The Discussion window
items.text:
The Discussion window shows its state ("Round 2 of 3", or why it ended), and each round with what each agent said, or that it has nothing to add.

  • Say something to everyone, then Say, adds your words.
  • End discussion ends it.

items.title: Observer
items.text: The Observer is a built-in role that never works on its own. When you switch it on, its model reads each sub-agent's report and says what the record shows of it.

items.title: Switching it on
items.text:
Settings › This project › Agents › Have a model look over each sub-agent's report.

That is one more model request after every sub-agent's report, on your plan or your bill. The Observer's model is sent the task, the report, the diffs of the changed files and the test's output, with the secrets KOLONİ knows masked. Choose its model on the Agents page, in the Observer role's panel.

items.title: What it does
items.text: It answers one question about a report, with no tools: what of the report the record shows, in a few sentences. No agent is opened.

items.title: How you see it
items.text:
In the agent's window, under its report, the Observer's words are tagged "opinion". If it could not answer, it says "no observation" and why.

The Orchestrator takes the Observer's words as an opinion, not a fact.

items.title: Recipe cookbook
items.text:
The ready recipes KOLONİ comes with. Ready recipes cannot be changed; press Copy it on the Recipes tab to make your own from one. "Review" means the step is done only when it has no findings. An in end takes the work into the project (on the Teams' work is ready card); a report end tells you what was found.

Recipe Steps Loops back Ends Feature Write the spec (Spec writer, asks you to approve) → Build it (Coder) → at once: Code review (Reviewer), Security review (Security reviewer), UI review (UI designer), Test it (Tester), all reviews reviews → Build it, 2 rounds in Bugfix Reproduce it (Debugger) → Fix it (Coder) → Test it (Tester, review) → Review it (Reviewer, review) review → Fix it, 2 rounds in Review only at once: Reviewer, Security reviewer, UI designer, all reviews — report Integration Learn (the team's experts) → Plan (Planner) → Experts check the plan (review) → Build (Coder) → Test (Tester, review) check → Plan, 2 rounds in Quality check Run the tests (Tester, review) → Find and fix the cause (Debugger, only if a problem was found) → at once: Code review (Reviewer), Security review (Security reviewer) fix → tests, 2 rounds report Model change Plan the experiment (Data scientist) → Experts review the plan (review) → Build it (ML engineer) → at once: Run the tests (Tester), Compare the metrics (Model evaluator) → Review it (Reviewer, review) experts → plan, 1 round; checks → build, 2 rounds in Pipeline change Change the pipeline (Data engineer) → at once: Run the tests (Tester), Check the data quality (Data analyst) → Review it (Reviewer, review) checks → change, 2 rounds in Infra change Change the infrastructure (DevOps) → at once: Security review (Security reviewer), Performance review (Performance engineer) → Review it (Reviewer, review) reviews → change, 2 rounds in Docs Write the docs (Docs writer) → Review it (Reviewer, review) review → write, 2 rounds in Research Find it out (Researcher) → Sum it up (Summarizer) — report Spec Break it into tasks (Product owner) → Write the spec (Spec writer) — report Analysis Analyse the data (Data analyst) → Review the analysis (Reviewer, review) — report Upkeep Update the dependencies (Dependency keeper) → Run the tests (Tester, review) → Find and fix the cause (Debugger, only if a problem was found) fix → tests, 2 rounds in Evolve Try it three ways (3 Coders as candidates, target score 80) try again, 3 rounds in

items.title: Which team runs which
items.text:
Each ready team has a ready recipe as its default: Web app runs Feature, Backend / API Bugfix, Quality Quality check, Product Spec, Data Analysis, Maintenance Upkeep, ML Model change, DataOps Pipeline change, DevOps Infra change, and Docs and Research the recipes of their names. You can change a team's Default recipe on the Agents page.

If you renamed or removed a ready recipe or team, yours may differ.

See Recipes and candidates.

items.title: Recipes and candidates
items.text:
A recipe is the drawn steps of a piece of work: who does each step, what runs at once, where it loops back and how it ends. "A chat's team runs by the recipe picked for it, else by its team's default." Recipes are on the Agents page, tab Recipes.

Teams, recipes, rooms and discussions in one picture.

items.title: Making a recipe
items.text:
• + Draw a new recipe starts an empty one.
  • Pick a ready recipe and press Copy it. Ready recipes cannot be changed: "A ready recipe: copy it to change it."
  • Or write it: describe the recipe in a sentence and press Make it a recipe. "The Orchestrator's model draws it on the board; nothing is saved until you save it."

The ready recipes include Feature, Bugfix, Review only, Integration, Quality check, Model change, Pipeline change, Infra change, Docs, Research, Spec, Analysis, Upkeep and Evolve.

items.title: The parts of a recipe
items.text:
The toolbar adds parts to the drawing: + Step, + All at once, + Loop back, + Room and + Ask me. Tidy up lays the drawing out again.

A step says who does it:

  • The Orchestrator picks;
  • The team's experts;
  • A role, with At most 1 to 5 agents;
  • Candidates (the best one goes on) (see below);
  • A team's stages.

A step can also have Done when, Only if the step before found a problem, If it fails (ask me or stop), and Ask me to approve its work before it goes on. That last one gives a card with Go on, Ask for changes and Stop.

All at once runs steps side by side. It waits for all branches or for the first one done.

Loop back goes back to an earlier step, at most 1 to 5 rounds.

Room puts 2 to 6 roles in one room. See Rooms.

Ask me is an end: Ask me, then in, or Tell me what was found. Every recipe needs an end.

items.title: Where a recipe is kept
items.text: Choose Kept in KOLONİ, for every folder, or Kept in this folder's .koloni/recipes (in git). A recipe kept in the folder travels with the project, but only recipes kept in KOLONİ can be picked under Teams for this chat or as a team's default.

items.title: How a recipe runs and ends
items.text:
The team works in one working copy, step by step, following the drawing. When the work reaches its end, the Teams' work is ready card asks whether to take it into the project: Take in, Fix the findings or Ask for changes. See Ready and approval cards.

At Full auto, the work is taken in without the card, unless a team failed or a check was skipped.

How a recipe runs, loops and ends. (full size)

items.title: Candidates
items.text:
A step whose Who is Candidates (the best one goes on) gives the same job to 2 to 5 agents. Each works in its own working copy. For their models choose Auto, the Lead picks, Same model or I pick each.

Each candidate's work is scored by the project's Measure command (Settings › This project › Checks and git): a command whose last line of output is a number from 0 to 100. A card then lists the scores and asks which candidate's work goes on. At Full auto the best score goes on by itself.

With a Target (0 to 100) and a loop, the step is tried again while the best score is below the target, and a new result replaces the kept one only if it scores higher. The ready recipe Evolve works this way: three Coders try the job, each their own way.

items.title: Roles
items.text: A role is what an agent is for: a description, instructions, the tools it may use and, if you like, its own model. Open Agents on the left rail ("Who does the work, in which teams, by which recipes"). The page has three tabs: Teams & roles, Recipes and History.

items.title: The roles
items.text:
The Orchestrator is the agent you talk to. It opens other roles as sub-agents when a part of the work needs them. KOLONİ comes with these roles:

Orchestrator, Planner, Coder, Tester, Reviewer, Researcher, Debugger, Architect, Security reviewer, Docs writer, Refactorer, UI designer, Data analyst, DevOps, Spec writer, Performance engineer, Database engineer, Dependency keeper, Translator, Summarizer, Product owner, Assistant product owner, Observer, Data engineer, ML engineer, Data scientist, Model evaluator, MLOps engineer, Designer, SEO specialist, Copywriter, Accessibility reviewer.

The Roles list on the Teams & roles tab shows them all. Filter roles… searches it, and the buttons All, In no team and Off narrow it. Each role has an on / off switch. The Orchestrator, the Planner and the Observer are always on.

items.title: A role's panel
items.text:
Click a role to open its panel. It has four tabs:

  • Overview: its category, the teams it is in, what it may do, and its Model as four answers: Which model, How hard it thinks, How much it reads and Who may move it (and Runs as where a role can run inside the CLI). Click an answer, or Edit, to change it.
  • Instructions: what the role is told.
  • Tools: the tools it may use, grouped (Files, Commands, Web, Browser, Team, To-do, Memory). A click switches a tool on or off and saves at once. A role needs at least one tool. Tools marked "asks" wait for your yes, as the chat's permission level says. Below, the MCP servers and skills the role has; you change those on the Tools page.
  • Knowledge: a switch for each Knowledge topic. On, choose Full ("its whole guide at each step") or Map ("its guide, read when its work touches it").

items.title: Editing a role
items.text:
Edit opens the role's form:

  • Name, and What it does: "The Orchestrator reads it to pick the role."
  • Category and Instructions.
  • Model: a card for each question. Each says one line; Learn more holds the rest.

Which model asks Who picks it?, then only what that choice needs:

Choice What it needs What it means Orchestrator From and to "It picks a tier for each job, inside this range, and says why." As the chat nothing "Whatever the chat's model picker says." One tier Fast, Balanced or Strongest "Always this tier. The Orchestrator can't change it." One model a Provider and a Model name "Always this model, whatever the job."

The Orchestrator itself has no Orchestrator choice. Try first lists up to 5 models from the team guide, tried in order before the choice above; + Add a model adds one. See Tiers.

How hard it thinks (Thinking) is Auto or One fixed level, and one ladder of the levels Off to Max:

  • Auto: the agent that opens a sub-agent picks a level for each task: Low for reading or summarizing, Medium for normal code, High for hard bugs or design. The levels it may pick are shaded, from Low up to the one marked most (High unless you move it, or the nearest lower level a model without High takes); click a level to move it. Its pick, and its reason, show under Details in the agent's window. Auto never picks Off. If it picks nothing, KOLONİ sends Medium (or the most, where that is lower), and the agent's window says "Thinking Medium, KOLONİ's default for Auto (the opener gave no level)".
  • One fixed level: every task gets the level you click, any level its model takes; the Orchestrator doesn't change it.

An agy model whose name ends in its level, such as gemini-3.8-flash-low, takes no other: it is sent none, and the agent's window says so. Under How hard it thinks, the role's Model card says "The model's own" and "its name sets its level: none is sent".

A role from before may still have a most next to a fixed level, or a most of Off under Auto. A line under the ladder says so ("The Orchestrator may also go up to High (set earlier)"), and Remove takes it away.

Struck levels are ones the role's model does not take, named under the ladder. A model without a level gets the nearest lower level it takes, never down to Off; one whose levels are not known gets none. Back to Auto, a most of Off, or one the model is known not to take, is taken away.

Nobody opens the Orchestrator, so it has no most: a click sets its level, and with Auto no level of its own is sent, and the chat's level, or the model's own, applies.

How much it reads (the context window) says the window found for its model, and where from. Past the % set in Settings › The app ("Summarise a long context at (%)") KOLONİ summarizes the older part, unless its CLI keeps its own session and does that itself. Where the window is unknown there is no fullness meter and nothing is summarized early. Set by hand takes a window of your own.

Who may move it: Any provider in the team guide, Only these, or No one. An agent that moves a sub-agent to another provider must say why.

Run inside the CLI: only when the agent that opens it runs in Claude Code. Cheaper, and counts toward no turn or role limit; it is not its own agent on the canvas, stops with the agent that opened it, and is never used while you're away or for a trigger.
