Not for the Orchestrator, the Observer or a team's lead. - It may: Read and search, Write code, Run commands, Use the web, or Pick tools one by one. - This role will sums up what the role will do, as you change the form.

Press Save. A built-in role has Reset to default; your own has Delete role.

items.title: A new role
items.text:
New role (on the Teams & roles tab) opens a form. "Agents in this role are opened by the Orchestrator or a team lead." Start from:

  • Blank;
  • An expert: it reads only; an expert changes nothing;
  • A copy of another role: it gets that role's servers, skills and knowledge, but not its teams.

Press Create role. An agent can also propose a role while it works; you decide on the Create this role? card.

items.title: History
items.text: The History tab shows what the roles, teams and recipes did in the Last 30 days or Last 7 days: how many agents were opened and ended done, and the team and recipe runs. Filter by role, team or recipe, or tick Failed only. Each row shows when, the role, the chat, the model and how it ended; click the chat to open it.

items.title: Rooms
items.text: A room is two to six agents working on one goal at the same time, in one working copy. They share the work out first, and each file has one holder. What one of them posts, the others read at their next step.

items.title: Opening a room
items.text:
Under More next to the message box, choose Work together… ("Open a room: two to six agents working on one goal at the same time"). Then:

  • Goal: what the room should do.
  • Members: a role for each, and its model. It starts with a Coder and a Reviewer. Add a member and Remove change the list.
  • What it may spend: posts by its members, tokens sent and written, and minutes. Empty means no limit. The room ends at the first limit it reaches.
  • These are this room's own. The project's default limits have one place: Settings › This project › New chats start with.

Press Open the room. The Orchestrator, a coordinator, or a recipe's Room part can open a room too. A room an agent opens gets at least 60,000 tokens, even if the agent asks for fewer. One member's step, with what it rereads, takes about 8,000 to 9,000 tokens, so a smaller budget would end the room before anyone posts. Tokens, at least in the same settings changes this number. If it is higher than Tokens, at most, the room gets the most.

Each project's default limits are under Settings › This project › New chats start with. A chat with no folder has no token limit for its rooms unless you set one when you open the room.

items.title: The room window
items.text:
The window is titled "Room · goal". It shows how much of its budget is used, the room's items, what was said, the reports, open questions, and what waits for you.

  • Post writes to the room.
  • Give it more adds posts, tokens or minutes to its budget.
  • Pause and Resume hold it and let it go on.
  • End ends it.
  • Let the Orchestrator follow: on, the Orchestrator reads what is said in the room, and may post, ask one more in, or end the room. Your words, Pause and End still come first. Off, it takes no part and is given the room's record when it is over.

A minimised room shows as a tab, "Room · goal · N posts".

items.title: Step limits
items.text: An agent works in steps. A sub-agent stops after a set number of them, so that no agent runs on without end. The Orchestrator counts no steps of its own: it stops when its work is done, when it goes round in circles, or at a limit you set. This page says where the limits are set, what happens when an agent reaches one, who may give it more, and what happens when nobody is there to ask.

items.title: What a step is
items.text:
A step is one request to the agent's model. The model answers, and may call tools: read a file, run a command, open a sub-agent. The tools run, and the next step reads what they gave back.

  • A CLI run One session per agent counts one step for each message it writes.
  • A CLI working with its own tools (Native) takes no steps KOLONİ can count: no step limit holds it. See Set up a CLI.

When an agent has two steps left, KOLONİ tells it to start nothing new, finish what it is on, and write its report: what it did and what is left.

items.title: Where the limits are set
items.text: Where What it sets Settings › The app › Agents › Steps an agent may take The most steps one sub-agent takes on a job: its task, or one later message it works on. 25 unless you change it, a whole number from 5 to 200. It holds in every project. It does not hold the Orchestrator. The role's form (Agents page) → Safety stops for one agent → At most this many steps A limit of the role's own. Where it is lower than the app's, it holds. It counts the steps an agent of the role takes on its work in the turn, and in the earlier turns it goes on from. Empty: only the app's limit. On the Lead role it is the Orchestrator's step limit; empty, it has none. Settings › This project › Limits and money › Continue gives this many more steps How many more steps Continue gives. 25 unless you change it, 1 to 200. A trigger's Model steps a run The steps of a whole turn a trigger starts, all its agents together. See Triggers.

items.title: More steps for coordinators
items.text: A team's coordinator needs steps to open its recipe's agents, wait, and read what comes back. It gets 4 more for each step of its recipe. Each Ask for changes that sends the recipe back gives that much again, for up to three rounds. With the app's 25, a coordinator whose recipe has six steps takes up to 49 steps. A role's own lower limit still holds over these.

items.title: The Orchestrator: no step count
items.text:
The Orchestrator runs the whole turn: it opens the teams, follows its rooms, passes messages on and writes the answer. A fixed count of its steps ran out on honest work, after the work was already in the project, so it has none. What stops it:

  • its work is done;
  • it goes round in circles (below);
  • a limit you set: the Lead role's At most this many steps, a trigger's Model steps a run for the whole turn;
  • in a turn nobody watches (a To-do task's, a job while you're away, a trigger's whose Minutes a run are longer): nothing has moved for Settings › The app › Stuck after this many minutes with no progress (30 unless you change it) - no file of the turn changed, no agent finished its work, no failing command passed. Each of those starts the minutes again, so honest work runs as long as it needs. They do not run out while a card waits for you, a command or a model step of the turn is under way, or an agent below the Orchestrator is at work;
  • a last resort: a To-do task's turn and a job while you're away end after An unattended turn runs at most (hours) (8 unless you change it; empty: no limit), however they go. A trigger's Minutes a run and a night's stop time hold as before;
  • either way the turn fails with the reason, its work kept - never cancelled: a To-do task gets its fix round, then is blocked, and the run goes on; a night tries the job once more, then goes on;
  • money and tokens, where you set them: the project's token limit for a message, its monthly budget, a night's money;
  • Stop.

A turn you started has no clock: you are there to press Stop, and the card below asks you.

items.title: When the Orchestrator goes round in circles
items.text:
KOLONİ watches the Orchestrator's tool calls. It stops it when:

  • the same call fails the same way 5 times, with no change of the turn and no command succeeding in between;
  • 10 calls in a row each repeat a call it had made, with the same result, since something last moved.

Something moves when a file of the turn changes, it opens an agent, or it sends a message to one it had not written to among its last three. A command that succeeds is judged by what it said, like any call. A call with other arguments, or one that gets a new result (a room's new post, a team's report), is new; the same call made several times in one step counts once. A wait in a room it follows counts as neither while it waits, however often it says the same; one back at once with the same words is a repeat. From the third repeat on, the Orchestrator is told what is repeating.

In a turn you started, the first time it is told, in its next step, to try a different approach or to report what it did and end. Its counts start again and it goes on; you see nothing. If it goes round in circles again, a card under the call asks you:

The Orchestrator has no step limit, and it seems to go round in circles: its last 10 calls each repeated one it had made, with the same result, with no change of this turn on record and no command of its own succeeding in between. Go on lets it carry on; Stop here ends it, with what it did so far. With no answer in 10 minutes its turn ends, its work kept.

  • Go on: it carries on, and the counts start again.
  • Stop here: the turn ends with that reason.
  • No answer in 10 minutes: the turn ends by itself. What is in the project stays, and work in agents' copies stays behind its cards, as at Stop. KOLONİ's line in the chat says how many agents it had opened, how many files it had changed in the project, and which call it repeated. A message you sent meanwhile, the To-do run or the night then goes on.

Either way the turn ends there: nothing more is waited for, and no other card comes. Where this turn's work is already in the project, it ends completed, not red, with KOLONİ's line saying why it ended; otherwise it fails with the reason.

The card waits for you at every level, Full auto too. As it goes up, KOLONİ tells you on the desktop and at the project's notification address, where you set them (Settings › This project): "The Orchestrator seems stuck: it repeated list_dir with the same result…".

In a turn nobody watches (a trigger's, a job while you're away, a To-do task) there is no card: the Orchestrator fails with the reason on record, also where it had written something - so a To-do task gets its fix round, then is blocked with why - and a night or the To-do run goes on with the next job or task.

items.title: At the limit
items.text: What happens depends on who stopped, which limit it reached, and whether it changed files.

items.title: The Orchestrator
items.text: The Orchestrator reaches a step limit only where you set one: its role's own, or a trigger's. It gets no Continue card there. If its teams are still at work it waits for them, then the turn ends. Send a message to go on.

items.title: A sub-agent with changed files
items.text:
A sub-agent that works in its own copy and has changed something stops at once. Its work is kept on a card in the chat ("Coder did not finish its work: this is what it had changed"), and nobody waits for it. While the turn runs, that card has Continue (+25 steps), with the project's Continue amount:

  • Continue gives it that many more steps, and it goes on in its kept copy. It gets the whole amount, also when it stopped at its role's own limit.
  • The card's other buttons decide the kept work, as on any card of changes.

If it stops again with changes, its card comes back with Continue. After the turn the card has no Continue: ask the Orchestrator in a new message to go on with it.

items.title: A sub-agent with nothing kept
items.text:
A sub-agent with no changes of its own, such as a team's coordinator or a reviewer, waits at the app's limit on a card under the call that opened it:

Reviewer came to its limit of 25 steps before its work was done. Continue gives it 25 more to go on where it is; Stop here ends it, with what it did so far.

  • Continue (+25 steps): it goes on where it is, with that many more steps. If its role has fewer steps left, the card offers only those.
  • Stop here: it ends with what it did so far. Its opener is told that you chose Stop here, and does not tell it to go on.

The card comes once for a job. After Continue the agent stops at the end of the steps it was given, with no new card.

There is no card when the agent stopped at its role's own limit, when its role has no steps left, or in the cases under When there is no card.

items.title: Who answers the card
items.text:
Level Who answers Ask before changes, Auto-edit files You. The turn waits for your answer. When you're away does not answer this card. Full auto The Orchestrator, at once: Continue or Stop here, with why. You see it under Decided for you. It answers once for each agent in a turn. The next time that agent reaches its limit in the turn, it gets no card and ends.

At Full auto the card still waits for you when:

  • the project is over its monthly budget;
  • the Orchestrator's provider is over its limit;
  • the turn is over the project's token limit;
  • the Orchestrator runs on a CLI and When you're away is Everything waits for you: each answer would use a request of your plan.

items.title: Going on by message
items.text:
The Orchestrator, or a team's coordinator, may tell an agent that stopped at a step limit to go on, with a message. This works at every level, once for each agent in a turn. The agent gets a new app step limit, not the Continue amount. Its role's own limit still holds: it stops there.

It is refused when:

  • you chose Stop here on the agent's card;
  • the agent already had more steps in this turn: Continue on its Continue / Stop here card, or an earlier go on;
  • the agent has no steps left under its role's own limit. A role's limit is your safety stop: only you give more past it, at every level, Full auto and work while you're away too. Press Continue on its kept work's card, or raise the role's limit. The Orchestrator is told "Coder is at its role's limit of 12 steps; more steps are the user's to give". While you're away nothing is given, and the job's report says the part is left undone.

items.title: When there is no card
items.text:
These get no Continue / Stop here card. The agent stops, and the agent that opened it is told what is left:

  • the Orchestrator itself, at a limit you set (its loop guard asks: see above);
  • a job of work while you're away;
  • a turn a trigger started: the trigger's Model steps a run holds for the whole turn, and it ends with "budget: stopped after {steps} model steps, the most this trigger gives a turn";
  • a To-do task's chat;
  • a room's members, and a room's sharing step (which has one step of its own);
  • an agent answering another agent's question, or working on another agent's message, a go on included: the sender waits for its reply;
  • an agent whose work is kept on a card with Continue;
  • an agent of a team you stopped.

items.title: Afterwards
items.text:
When a sub-agent stops at a step limit, its opener is told that its part is not done. It hands what is left to another agent, tells it to go on where it may, or says in its answer what is left undone.

On the canvas the agent's box says "Stopped at its step limit". Where it had more, it says "Stopped after the {n} steps it was given": {n} is the job's whole count, so after a Continue of 25 at 25 steps it reads 50.

To give it more:

  • while the turn runs, Continue on its kept work's card;
  • after the turn, ask the Orchestrator in your next message to go on with it. That is a new turn, so the once-a-turn go on is there again for an agent that stopped at the app's limit or at the end of the steps it was given;
  • an agent that stopped at its role's own limit counts the steps it took before, in later turns too: raise the role's At most this many steps first, then ask the Orchestrator to go on. A raised limit holds from its next job;
  • for work that is always big, raise Steps an agent may take: it holds every sub-agent.

items.title: One job, three ways
items.text:
A Reviewer has to read a large change. It needs about 35 steps. The app's limit is 25, Continue gives 25, and the Reviewer role has no limit of its own.

In the day, at Ask before changes. At 23 steps the Reviewer is told it has two left. At 25 it stops, and the card asks you. Continue gives it 25 more; it goes on where it is and ends at about 35. Stop here ends it with what it found so far, and the Orchestrator's answer says what was not reviewed.

In the day, at Full auto. The same card comes, and the Orchestrator answers it at once, say with Continue. Its answer and why show under Decided for you. The Reviewer ends at about 35. Had it needed more than 50, it would stop at 50 with no new card, and the Orchestrator would say what is left; more steps are then yours to give in your next message.

While you're away. No card. The Reviewer stops at 25, and the job's Orchestrator is told its part is not done. It may tell the Reviewer once to go on: the Reviewer gets 25 new steps and ends at about 35. Had it needed more than 50, it would stop again, and the job's report would say what is left undone. The job can still count as done when you're back: open its chat to read what was left.

items.title: Teams
items.text: A team is a named group of roles, set out in stages. A role can be in more than one team. Teams are on the Agents page, tab Teams & roles.

items.title: The ready teams
items.text:
KOLONİ comes with these teams: Web app, Backend / API, Data, Docs, DevOps, Quality, Research, Product, Maintenance, ML and DataOps. You can change them, or make your own with New team.

To build a website, the Web app team also has a Copywriter for the site's words and an SEO specialist in Build, and an Accessibility reviewer in Check: the SEO specialist makes the site easy to find, the reviewer checks it is easy to use with a keyboard or a screen reader.

items.title: Stages
items.text:
A team starts with four stages: Plan, Build, Check and Write & keep up. Drag a role from the role list into a stage. You can rename, move or remove a stage (one must stay), and add one with + Add a stage. Each stage has an "all at once" box for roles that work at the same time.

Each team also has a Default recipe, the recipe it runs by unless a chat picks another, and The Orchestrator may pick it.

items.title: Coordinators
items.text: Each team has its own lead, shown as "Team coordinator". It "steps in only when this team works beside another team; else the Orchestrator runs it." Switched off, the Orchestrator always runs that team itself.

items.title: Teams for a chat
items.text:
On the canvas, Teams for this chat chooses how the chat uses teams:

Mode What it does Orchestrator decides "It picks the teams and a recipe for each, and says why." Manual "You pick the teams it may use; it opens only those a message needs." For each team, pick its default recipe, No recipe, or another recipe. + Add a team with a recipe adds one. No teams "As before: it calls any role itself."

Use for new chats in this project keeps the choice for the project's new chats (Settings › This project → New chats start with shows and changes it). Plan first is the switch under the message box, not here. While a team runs, Stop stops it and Finish now ends it with what it has.

items.title: A team that was not opened
items.text: In Manual, a turn that did work may open some of the teams you gave the chat and not others. The Orchestrator is first told once to open the missing team or say why not. If it still does not, a line at the turn's end says so, just above the Orchestrator's answer: "Quality was not opened in this turn." (or "… were not opened in this turn." for several). It is not on the Teams' work is ready card. A turn that opened none of them, because the Orchestrator answered itself, gets no such line.

items.title: Waiting for another team
items.text:
An agent of one team, its coordinator for example, can wait for the work of another team of the chat that has a coordinator: a file or an endpoint it needs. Waiting spends none of its steps, and it holds no place among the agents at work: its box says it is waiting.

  • When the other team's work in this turn has ended, the waiting agent is told how it ended, its coordinator's report and the files it changed.
  • When a message reaches the waiting agent, the wait ends there: it is told a message came, reads it, and may wait again.
  • One wait lasts at most 10 minutes. After that the agent is told the other team is still at work, and may wait again, go on without it, or end with what is left undone.
  • An agent waits at most three times in a turn.
  • Two teams cannot wait for each other: the second is told to do its part first.
  • A team not opened in this turn has nothing to wait for.
  • Stop on the waiting team ends the wait, and its work.

See Step limits for what a coordinator does when its steps run out.

A team at work: its frame on the canvas fills as its recipe runs.

The Web app team at work: its frame holds the recipe's steps and the Coder, and Ready for you waits at the end.

Only recipes kept in KOLONİ are offered here, not a folder's own recipes.

See Recipes and candidates.

items.title: Which way to work
items.text: KOLONİ offers several ways to get work done, from one message to a list of jobs while you are away. Start with the smallest that fits: every extra agent is more model calls, so more tokens, money or plan use.

items.title: At a glance
items.text: You want… Use… Because… What it costs a small, clear job done just ask, in a chat the Orchestrator does small jobs itself, or opens one sub-agent the fewest calls to see the plan before anything changes Plan first each message first gets a plan to approve one planning pass more a bigger piece of work, built, reviewed and tested a team with a recipe the recipe runs the steps in order, loops back on findings, and asks you where the recipe says (Feature: the spec, and the work at the end) one agent per step, more for each loop two or more agents to build one thing at the same time a room its members share the work out, each file has one holder, and they read each other's posts each member's calls, up to the room's budget agents to think a question through, with nothing changed a discussion agents talk in rounds and nobody writes anything each speaker's whole work so far is sent again at each step, so tokens grow faster than the talk the best of several attempts Evolve, or another recipe with Candidates 2 to 5 agents try the same job, each is scored by your measure command, and the best goes on each candidate in each round, plus the measure runs two models' answers side by side Compare one message goes to two models, and you keep one's work two runs of the message several jobs done while you are away work while you're away each job runs in its own copy, and you decide when you're back what comes in each job, within the card's money limit the same job by the clock, or when files change a trigger it starts a turn by itself, with only the permissions you ticked each run, within the trigger's budget a list of tasks worked through in order To-do each task runs in a chat of its own, one after another each task's turn

items.title: Examples
items.text:
"Fix the failing date test." Just ask. One bug in one place is a job for the Orchestrator, or one Coder it opens. With Teams for this chat → No teams, it never brings in a team.

"Add a password reset page, with review and tests." A team with the Feature recipe: in Teams for this chat choose Manual, then the Web app team, whose default recipe is Feature. A Spec writer writes the spec for you to approve, a Coder builds it, then a Reviewer, a Security reviewer, a UI designer and a Tester check it at once; findings go back to the Coder, at most twice. You take the work in on the Teams' work is ready card. See A web app with a team.

"Fix this crash, and make sure it stays fixed." The Bugfix recipe: in Teams for this chat choose Manual, then the Backend / API team, whose default recipe is Bugfix. A Debugger reproduces the crash, a Coder fixes it, a Tester and a Reviewer check it. Cheaper than Feature: four steps, no spec and fewer reviews.

"The backend and frontend teams must agree the API first." A room. Open one with Work together… under More, or ask the Orchestrator to bring the teams' leads together in a room before the teams start. They agree the shape in the room, then each team builds its side. See Rooms.

"Should we keep SQLite or move to Postgres?" A discussion. Ask the Orchestrator to have the Architect and a Database engineer discuss it. Nobody changes anything; you can join in and end it. Set a token limit under Settings › This project › Limits and money › A discussion's tokens, at most. See Discussions.

"Make this function faster, and keep the fastest version." Evolve. First set a Measure command (Settings › This project › Checks and git) whose last line is a score from 0 to 100. Evolve has three Coders try the job, each their own way, and tries again while the best score is under 80, for at most four rounds. That is up to twelve Coders: the most expensive way on this page. See Picking the best of several candidates.

"Run the tests every night and tell me what failed." A trigger: By the clock, At a time of day, with the message "Run the tests and say what failed". It may only do what you tick. A recipe does not run in a trigger's turn, and a trigger never starts a CLI that works with its own tools. See Triggers.

"While I'm away tonight: update the dependencies, tidy the docs, and add tests to the parser." Work while you're away. Ask the Orchestrator to plan the jobs; it proposes the jobs on a While you're away card, with a money limit and, if you want one, a stop time. Leave KOLONİ running: closing it ends the jobs. See A job while you're away.

items.title: The ready recipes
items.text: KOLONİ comes with these recipes: Feature, Bugfix, Review only, Integration, Quality check, Model change, Pipeline change, Infra change, Docs, Research, Spec, Analysis, Upkeep and Evolve. The Recipe cookbook lists each one's steps and which team runs it by default.

items.title: Keeping the cost down
items.text:
• Start small. A single agent that is not enough can still hand work on; a team that was too much has already spent.
  • Review only and Research report what they found and change nothing.
  • A discussion and a room have budgets: set them before you start.
  • Give roles a tier, so easy jobs go to a fast model. See Tiers and Agents may use and Keeping costs down.

items.title: Answering for you
items.text: When you are away, questions can wait for you, or the Orchestrator can answer the safe ones itself.

items.title: Switching it on
items.text:
Settings › This project › Asking and away › When you're away:

  • Everything waits for you (the default);
  • The Orchestrator answers what it safely can, after a number of minutes (0 to 1440; 10 unless you change it).

With the second, once you have not answered for that many minutes, or the away card is on, "the Orchestrator picks, says why, and you see it under "Decided for you"". During work while you're away it answers at once.

"An Orchestrator on a CLI uses one request of your plan for each answer."

items.title: What it may decide
items.text:
Only:

  • an agent's question to you;
  • a recipe's "Ask me";
  • opening a sub-agent on its role's own model, while that provider has room.

items.title: What always waits for you
items.text:
Commands, file changes, the web, installing, secrets, folders, new roles or skills, deleting, Take in, Discard, Commit, a different model that may cost money, and Stop. It also does not answer when the turn is over its token limit, the project is over its monthly budget, or the provider is over its limit.

In To-do task chats it never answers for you.

items.title: Decided for you
items.text:
What it answered shows under Decided for you while you were away: who asked, what the Orchestrator chose, and why. Press OK to keep it, or Change → to give another answer. If the answer cannot be undone any more, it says so.

At Full auto the Orchestrator also answers questions in a chat you watch, at once, and some of KOLONİ's own cards, such as an agent's Continue / Stop here card at its step limit; those answers show under the same heading. Full auto alone does not let it open a sub-agent for you, and it does not answer those cards during work while you're away. An Orchestrator on a CLI answers at Full auto only where When you're away is set to The Orchestrator answers what it safely can.

items.title: The same question again
items.text: If the same agent asks the same question again in the turn, with the same words and choices, it gets the Orchestrator's earlier answer at once, with no new request. Its line under Decided for you says it is "its answer when this was asked before". If you changed that answer, your answer is the one given.

items.title: Work while you're away
items.text:
Before you leave, the Orchestrator can plan jobs for while you are away: for an hour, an afternoon or the night. Each job works in its own copy of the project, so your project does not change while you are gone. When you are back you decide what comes in.

Work while you're away (below) and triggers (above): work that runs while nobody watches.

items.title: Planning the jobs
items.text:
Tell the Orchestrator you are going away (to sleep, out, for a while) and what it should work on meanwhile. It does none of that work itself. It puts the jobs on a While you're away card instead, and nothing starts before your Start.

Only the Orchestrator plans these jobs, in a turn you started, in a chat with a folder, where it keeps the To-do list. It does not plan them in a Plan first turn, nor while jobs of the project run while you're away. A newer card takes the place of one not started yet.

items.title: The jobs
items.text:
A card has 1 to 10 jobs, in the order they run. Each job has:

  • a title, one plain line of at most 200 characters;
  • optionally, what makes it done;
  • optionally, a team, and a recipe for it; without a recipe the team works by its default recipe. A recipe with no team is not used.

items.title: The card
items.text:
The card says "The Orchestrator's jobs for while you're away: change anything before you start."

  • "Each job works in its own copy. Your project does not change while you're away; you take the work in when you're back."
  • "If a job needs your word, it waits and the next one goes on." See Questions and approvals.
  • What is kept out: files or folders of the project no job may change.
  • When to stop: Stop at a time, or after spending an amount, whichever comes first. By default there is no time limit and no spend limit: the jobs run until they are done. Set a time or an amount (in the currency of your prices) on the card, or tell the Orchestrator, if you want one. If the project has a monthly budget, the jobs spend at most what is left of it. Empty a field and that limit is off; the card says "(empty: no time limit)" and "(empty: no spend limit)". On a provider paid by plan no money is counted, and the card says so: "there only the time holds". Your provider limits hold too.
  • A job works as long as it makes progress. Once nothing has moved for Settings › The app › Stuck after this many minutes with no progress (30 unless you change it) - no file of the job changed, no agent finished its work, no failing command passed - it fails with that reason, is tried once more, and the next one goes on. As a last resort a job stops after An unattended turn runs at most (hours) (8 unless you change it; empty: no limit), what it did kept in its copy; on the report it is under Could not be done, with "Stopped after 8 hours, the most one job works".

Change the list lets you edit each job and what makes it done, take a job out (one must stay), add one with + Add a job (up to 10), and change what is kept out: up to 20 files or folders of the project, one a line or with commas between. Name the file or folder itself: a pattern such as src/* or a place outside the project is refused. Then Save the list, or Cancel.

Start starts the jobs; they go onto the To-do list too. Not now puts the card away. Start is refused while Stop everything holds (press Resume first), and while a To-do task is at work.

The card can also offer Let the Orchestrator answer what it safely can. It turns on the project's When you're away setting, which then stays on after the jobs; change it back under Settings › This project › Asking and away. See Answering for you.

items.title: How the jobs run
items.text:
Jobs run one at a time, in the card's order. Each starts in a new chat named after it, its first message the job and what makes it done, and works in a copy of the project of its own.

  • Level and model: the job's chat has the permission level and the model of the chat where the card was, not the To-do page's run settings. Its other settings are the project's, as in any chat: who changes the files, opening sub-agents, and the rest.
  • Team and recipe: a job with a team works in Manual with that team, by the recipe the card gave.
  • The copy leaves out .git/, build/, dist/ and caches, and shares node_modules/, .venv/ and venv/ with the project. A job that needs what is not in the copy changes nothing and waits for you, its report ending "Needs the project itself: …".
  • A job that fails is tried once more in its chat. Failed twice, it could not be done, and the next one goes on.
  • A job that waits for your word waits, and the next one goes on.

The top bar shows "☾ Away · job 2 of 4" with Stop all, and "· until 07:00" after it when the card has a stop time. The To-do page shows the jobs too: since when, what they spent against the limit, and each job as it stands, with what its agents are doing right now. A job's chat says at the top when its jobs started, with a link back to their report.

items.title: Stricter rules while you're away
items.text:
• Commands follow the job chat's level. Below Full auto, a command no rule covers waits for you, and the job with it. At every level these wait too: a command that deletes, overwrites or sends something off the machine; one that hands a command to a shell or another program; and one that installs into the project's shared dependency folders.
  • Ordinary file changes in the job's copy never ask: they are kept for your Take in. Files that steer agents, secret files and places outside the project wait for you as in a watched turn, and the job with them.
  • Kept-out places: a write to one, or a command that names one, is refused, and the try is on the report.
  • No MCP server tools are used.
  • CLIs: a CLI working with its own tools that is not started in the job's copy, or not held to it (Copilot working Native, agy when it may write), cannot work on a job: "… cannot work on a job while you're away".
  • At Full auto the Orchestrator does not answer KOLONİ's own cards while you're away, as it does while you watch.

items.title: Questions and approvals
items.text:
What needs your word waits for you, and the job waits with it. The next job goes on meanwhile.

With When you're away set to The Orchestrator answers what it safely can, the Orchestrator answers at once while the jobs run, without waiting the minutes you set. It answers only an agent's question, a recipe's "Ask me", and opening a sub-agent on its role's own model; it does not answer once the project is over its monthly budget or a provider is over its limit. Everything else waits: commands and changes that ask, the web, secrets, folders, new roles and skills. See Answering for you.

A job that waits is shown under Waits for your word, on the report and in Ready for you.

items.title: Step limits while away
items.text:
Nobody is there to answer a Continue / Stop here card, so none comes:

  • A sub-agent that reaches its step limit stops. The job's Orchestrator is told its part is not done, and may tell it once to go on, with a new step limit.
  • One that stopped at its role's own limit, or stops again, ends. The job's Orchestrator hands what is left to another agent, or says in its report what is left undone. The job can still count as done: read its chat.
  • The job's Orchestrator counts no steps. If it goes round in circles (the same call failing the same way 5 times, or 10 calls in a row bringing nothing new), the job fails with that reason, is tried once more in its chat, and the night goes on with the next job.

See Step limits.

items.title: What stops the jobs
items.text:
The jobs end when:

  • every job was tried;
  • the card's stop time comes, if it has one ("Stopped at 07:00, the time you set.");
  • they have spent their money ("Stopped at 5.02 of 5.00 USD, the spend limit.");
  • the project is over its monthly budget, or the Orchestrator's provider is over its limit, when the next job is about to start;
  • you press Stop all ("Stopped by you.");
  • KOLONİ is closed ("Stopped: KOLONİ was closed while you were away.");
  • the next job cannot start.

The time and the money are checked before each model step. A clock also watches the stop time and each job's hours at most, so a long command is cut at them too. Its minutes with nothing moving do not run out while a command or a model step of it is under way, an agent below the Orchestrator is at work, or it waits for your word: those have limits of their own. When the jobs stop, the job at work stops, its work kept in its copy, and is shown as Stopped. A job that waits for your word goes on waiting. When KOLONİ is closed, the jobs at work and those that wait count as could not be done: answer what waits before you close KOLONİ.

Stop everything in the top bar holds the jobs instead of ending them: the job at work and a job that waits for your word are stopped, the next job waits for Resume, and the card's time and money still end them.

A trigger's budget plays no part here: these jobs are not trigger turns.

If you set up notifications, you get one when the jobs end.

items.title: When you're back
items.text:
KOLONİ opens on the report on the canvas until you have seen it. The chat where the card was has one line, such as "While you were away: 3 done, 1 waits - on the canvas".

The report shows when the jobs ran, what they spent and why they ended; nothing of it is in your project before you take it in. Its sections are Done, Waits for your word, Could not be done, Stopped, Not started, Proposed while you were away, not started (with Add to To-do or Dismiss) and Kept out, as you asked (what tried to change those places, refused).

Each job row says what its reviews found, and warns where its copy changed a place you kept out, or a file another job changed too. A job that changed nothing is "Done, nothing changed". For each job:

  • Allow and go on or Refuse, when it waits for a command, a change, a web request or an agent to open. A question, a folder or a secret is answered in its chat: Open its chat. The job then goes on in its copy.
  • Take in brings its work into the project; Take in all takes in every done job's work. Where two jobs changed one file, the two are joined line by line where their lines do not clash. A clashing line is not taken: the card of the job's kept copy, in its chat, decides it.
  • Try again, for a job that could not be done or was stopped, once the jobs are over. It runs in the job's chat as an ordinary turn, not in a copy: its changes go into the project as that chat's level says.
  • See the changes or Open its chat.

The To-do page shows the same jobs, open by itself while a job needs a decision of yours.

See A job while you're away for the steps from planning to taking the work in.

items.title: To-do
items.text: The To-do page holds a project's tasks, in your order. "Each task runs in its own chat; you decide when it is done." Open To-do on the left rail.

items.title: Adding tasks
items.text:
Type in Add a task — title, then Enter. Once there is a title you can also set its Priority (high, normal, low), a Detail and Done when (optional), then press Add task.

A rough note can become several tasks. Type it, for example "the login page is broken on mobile, and we need a password reset", and press Write it with the Product owner. A model writes it as tasks, each with a title, detail, done when and priority. It is asked once, with no tools: your first fast model if you have one, else the Orchestrator's. The line under the buttons says which model writes them and whether the request costs money. The tasks appear under the box for you to change. Press Add on one, ✕ to drop one, or Add all. Nothing is saved until you add it. Plan it in a chat works the other way: it opens a chat in the project whose first message asks for the Product owner. The Product owner reads the project and proposes tasks, which wait for you like any agent's.

A rough note written as two tasks by Write it with the Product owner; nothing is saved until you add one.

Agents with the To-do tools (the Product owner and the Assistant product owner) can propose tasks and changes. They wait for you under Waiting for you:

What waits Buttons A new task an agent proposed Add / Edit / Reject A task an agent thinks is done ("done?") Done / Not yet A change an agent proposed Change / Reject

When several new tasks wait, Approve all adds them all. Edit opens the task's title and detail; change them, then press Add.

items.title: Follow-up tasks
items.text:
After a turn in one of the project's chats, the Assistant PO suggests what to do next. It looks at the turn's record: work left undone or for later, a TODO, a step that failed. It proposes at most three tasks, each with the words they came from ("Proposed by the Assistant PO, from: ..."). Those words must be an agent's in that turn, or the first line of a step that failed, not your message. Backticks, * and _ are ignored, and curly quotes count as straight ones, so `CHANGELOG.md` still matches CHANGELOG.md. A suggestion without such words is dropped. So is one that looks like a task already on the list, or one you rejected before. Each one dropped is written, with why, to runtime/logs/koloni.log, and shows in the Inspector of its canvas box (below). The suggestions wait under Waiting for you like any agent's. An added task starts when you press Run the backlog, or by itself where the To-do list runs by itself. A suggestion whose words look like they try to give the agent orders says so on its row.

It is one small model request, with no tools, after each turn that did something: changed a file, ran a command, handed work to a sub-agent or had a step fail. A turn that only answered asks nothing. It is made once the turn is over, so your next message does not wait for it. It goes to the first model of the fast tier, or of the tier you chose. It skips a provider that is down, at its limit, out of its plan, or whose pay-per-token use you refused in that turn. With no such model nothing is suggested. The model is sent what was said in the turn, the files it changed, the steps that failed and the open tasks' titles. The secrets KOLONİ knows, and the variables the project passes to its commands, are masked. Jobs while you're away and triggers get suggestions too; rooms, discussions and To-do tasks' own turns get none. Nothing is asked while the project is over its monthly budget.

Each request shows on the canvas as an Assistant PO box under the turn, on a dashed line down from the Orchestrator: the model, "2 proposed · 1 dropped" (at Full auto also "Orchestrator added 1"), its tokens ("–" where not reported), and To-do →. Click it to see why each suggestion was dropped; a double click, or To-do →, opens this page. A request that failed or timed out says "Sent, not heard out". A turn where it was not asked has no such box.

At Full auto, in a turn you started, you are not asked. The Orchestrator's model decides each suggestion, add or reject, with one more request, and says why in one sentence. You see its word under Decided for you in the chat. OK keeps it; Change undoes it while the task is still todo. A task it added does not start, by Run the backlog or by itself, until you press OK, there or under Waiting for you on the To-do page. One it rejected stays on the To-do page, folded under Rejected by the Orchestrator, with Add. It is not asked when the provider has no room left on its plan, or when the To-do list runs by itself. Nor is it asked when the Orchestrator runs on a CLI and the project does not let it answer while you're away. It never adds a suggestion whose words look like orders. Suggestions from jobs while you're away and from triggers always wait for you.

Turn it off, or choose the tier, in Settings › This project › Agents.

items.title: Your tasks
items.text:
Your tasks lists them by priority, then in your order. Drag a task, or use ⋯ → move up / move down. The ⋯ menu also has Edit, Waits for ("it starts once these are done") and Delete.

A task's state shows as a tag, such as queued, running, "needs you", "needs you · Take in", stuck, or done.

items.title: Running tasks
items.text:
Run the backlog starts the next tasks. Runs by itself keeps starting them, one after another. Each task runs in a new chat, with the task as its first message. At most two run at once.

"A task not finished gets one fix round; still not, it is stuck and the next goes on." When an agent thinks a task is done, it waits as "done?" for your word.

A task's turn works as long as it makes progress. Once nothing has moved for Settings › The app › Stuck after this many minutes with no progress (30 unless you change it) - no file of the turn changed, no agent finished its work, no failing command passed - it stops, its work kept, and counts as not finished: its fix round comes, then it is stuck and the next task goes on. The same happens, as a last resort, after An unattended turn runs at most (hours) (8 unless you change it; empty: no limit). Its Orchestrator also stops if it goes round in circles: see Step limits.

Nothing starts while one of your own turns is at work, while everything is paused, during work while you're away, or over the project's monthly budget.

items.title: Run settings
items.text:
Run settings sets the level of the task chats (Ask before changes, Auto-edit files or Full auto), Who changes the files, and the Provider and Model name.

Task chats follow some extra rules: a CLI that works with its own tools does not run them; commands that delete, overwrite or send something off the machine, or that hand a command to a shell, ask at every level; and the Orchestrator never answers for you in them.

items.title: Triggers
items.text:
A trigger starts work by itself: by the clock, when files change, or when a program on this machine calls it. "Only you make or change a trigger; no agent can." Open Triggers on the left rail.

A trigger's run is a turn nobody watches. There is nobody to ask, so it may do only what the trigger allows. Everything else is refused, not asked.

Triggers and work while you're away: work that runs while nobody watches.

items.title: Making a trigger
items.text:
Press New trigger and pick a ready one, or Start from blank:

  • Keep an agent on this project (every hour, reads only);
  • Every morning: summarise the work since the last working day;
  • When source files change: run the tests;
  • Every Friday at 17:00: check the dependencies.

The form:

  • Name.
  • Starts: By the clock, When files change or On a request from outside. This cannot be changed later.
    • By the clock: At an interval (Every so many minutes, at least 5; the first run starts at once), or At a time of day (a Time by this machine's clock, and Days: every day, weekdays, or chosen days).
    • When files change: a Path pattern in the project, such as src/**/*.py. "It runs ten seconds after the last change." Folders such as .git and node_modules are never watched.
    • On a request from outside: see Webhooks.
  • Conversation: the chat it runs in. While that chat is at work, a run that falls due is skipped.
  • Message: "What the agent is told each time, as if you had written it."

items.title: What its work may do without asking
items.text:
"There is nobody to ask when it runs." The chat's own permission level does not apply. Tick what it may do:

Choice What it allows May change files Writing files in the project. May run these commands The commands you tick, each run exactly as written, with no extra arguments. Ticked from the chat's list of commands that run without asking. Add to the list adds one; that also lets the chat's own messages run it without asking. May open sub-agents 0 to 4 per run. May search the web Web searches. May make requests to these hosts Plain GET and HEAD requests, to hosts ticked from the chat's allowed list. May send you notifications Notifications, where you set an address.

The project's own test command also runs without being ticked.

items.title: Budget and end
items.text:
• Model steps a run (default 15), Minutes a run (default 10), Runs a day (default 24). Model steps a run counts all the turn's agents together, the Orchestrator too: it is the step limit you set for the turn. Where Minutes a run is longer than Settings › The app › Stuck after this many minutes with no progress, its turn also ends once nothing has moved for that long; and it ends if the Orchestrator goes round in circles: see Step limits. "Three runs in a row that fail or go over switch the trigger off."
  • Ends: No end, After so many runs, or After a day.
  • Run once when KOLONİ starts if a run was missed (on by default).
  • Run even if nothing changed (clock only). Without it, in a git project, a run is skipped when nothing changed since the last one.

Press Add trigger.

items.title: The trigger's card
items.text:
Each trigger is a card: when it runs, what it is told, what it may do, its budget and its last run. It has an on / off switch, Run now, its recent runs, and a ⋯ menu with Edit, New key (for webhooks) and Delete.

A trigger's card: when it runs, what it is told, what it may do and its budget.

items.title: Webhooks
items.text:
A trigger that starts On a request from outside runs when a program on this machine sends a POST request to its address. After you save it, the page shows the address once: copy it, then press I have copied it. "If it is lost or leaks, make a new key on the trigger; this address then stops working." ⋯ → New key → Make a new key makes a new address; the old one stops at once.

Only requests from this machine are accepted. What the request carries (at most 4000 characters) is given to the agent as something to look at, never as an instruction.

items.title: When a run needed something it was not allowed
items.text: A run's record shows It would have asked you: and what was refused. "Each was refused, and nothing was done in its place." Allow this in the trigger opens the trigger's form with that ticked; it is yours to save.

items.title: What a trigger's run never does
items.text:
• It never asks you anything.
  • It does not run on a CLI that works with its own tools (Native, or agy). A trigger on a chat whose Orchestrator would run on one is not saved, and the form says why.
  • It never moves to a provider that is paid per token.
  • It does not read secret files, write files that steer agents, go outside the project, or use MCP tools.
  • It puts nothing forward for the project's memory core.

items.title: Pausing every trigger
items.text:
The top bar shows how many triggers are on, with Pause all. Paused, it says "Triggers paused", with Resume. Pause holds every trigger of every project and stops the runs at work.

To keep triggers from starting by themselves at all, start KOLONİ with KOLONI_TRIGGER_CLOCK=0.

items.title: Triggers proposed by agents
items.text: An agent can propose a trigger on a Make this trigger? card. A proposal only reads, opens no sub-agents, and has the default budget. "Approve makes it as shown; to let it do more, or change anything, Edit." Agents can propose clock and file triggers only, never webhooks.

items.title: Architecture
items.text:
KOLONİ is one Python process that serves a React page and an HTTP API on 127.0.0.1, keeps its data in SQLite, and runs agents as asyncio tasks.

What runs where. The diagrams' sources are in docs/diagrams/, with a README on editing them.

items.title: Backend (app/)
items.text:
• main.py builds the app. At the start it applies a staged restore, backs up and migrates the database, tidies it, marks work that was cut off as interrupted, seeds the built-in roles and the first providers, and sets the page key. It serves the built page from frontend/dist on the same origin. FastAPI's own docs pages are switched off.
  • api/: the HTTP routes, all under /api.
  • agent/: the agent runner. AgentRunner runs one turn per asyncio task. It is split into mixins (spawning sub-agents, cards and approvals, memory, limits, rooms, discussions, work while you're away and more); the package docstring lists them.
  • Model clients: model_client.py (OpenAI-compatible), model_anthropic.py (the Anthropic Messages API), model_cli.py (a CLI as one step per model step), model_session.py (a CLI session whose only tools are KOLONİ's, over MCP), model_native.py (a CLI with its own tools), model_agy.py (agy). providers.py chooses which one runs a role.
  • db/ and alembic/: SQLAlchemy models and migrations. The database is backed up before a migration.
  • workspace.py: file access confined to the project folder and the folders the user opens.
  • copies.py: each sub-agent works in its own copy, outside the project; its changes come back by a three-way merge.
  • commands.py, command_runner.py, executors/: which commands ask, and running them on this machine or in Docker.
  • triggers.py: clock, file-change and webhook turns.
  • mcp_client.py: the client for the user's MCP servers. mcp_bridge.py: the small program a CLI starts as its MCP server, which relays to KOLONİ's own tools.

items.title: Frontend (frontend/)
items.text: React, Vite, React Flow (the canvas) and Zustand (the store, src/state/store.ts). src/api/generated.ts holds the API's types, generated from the backend's schema by scripts/export_openapi.py; after changing an API shape, run npm run generate:api in frontend/.

items.title: How the page talks to the API
items.text:
Every /api request carries the page key in the X-KOLONI-Key header (or ?key= for event streams and downloads). The page takes the key from the link KOLONİ prints, or swaps a one-time code for it, and keeps it in the browser's local storage. A few doors need no key: the health check, webhooks, Claude Code's status line, and the one-time code exchange.

Events reach the page over server-sent events, per conversation.

items.title: How a turn flows
items.text:
1. The page posts a message to the conversation.
  2. The server records it and starts a run as an asyncio task.
  3. The Orchestrator (the Lead role) works with its tools and may open sub-agents, each in a working copy.
  4. Anything that needs the user becomes a card; the run waits for the answer.
  5. A finished sub-agent's changes are taken into the project, or put before the user on a card first.
  6. Every step is recorded, and the canvas draws the turn from that record.

The same turn, step by step: where it waits for you, and how the page hears of each step.

A message's journey, from Send to the chat and the canvas. (full size)

items.title: The data model
items.text:
The database is SQLite, its tables in app/db/models.py. A project has chats; a chat has turns (runs); a turn has agents, and an agent has messages, tool calls, file changes, commands and take-ins (merges). Memory, knowledge, to-do tasks and triggers belong to a project; providers, roles, teams and recipes are the same for every project. Working copies are folders, not rows.

The main tables, their keys and how they link. (full size)

items.title: Inside the agent runner
items.text:
app/agent/ holds AgentRunner, built from mixins, one per part. A turn picks its model by tier, then loops: in step mode KOLONİ builds the history (compacting it when it is too long), asks the model, and runs each tool call it asks for. A CLI in session or native mode keeps the loop itself. Limits, slots, observing, recording and the rest work around every step.

The agent runner's parts and how a step flows through them. (full size)

items.title: Contributing (DCO)
items.text:
• Sign off every commit (Developer Certificate of Origin): git commit -s.
  • CLA: a pull request agrees to the short-form CLA.md in the repository, which lets the project relicense the contribution. KOLONİ is AGPL-3.0-or-later.
  • Keep a change small and focused, and deliver a behaviour end to end: backend and page together.
  • scripts/verify.ps1 must pass. See Tests and verify.
  • Review the staged diff before you commit. Never add secrets, caches or runtime/ output.
  • Check the licence of any source code or asset before you take it.
  • No fake agents, progress or usage: a value KOLONİ does not know stays unknown.

items.title: The changelog
items.text:
CHANGELOG.md is in English and every release looks the same:

  • One heading per version: ## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD. Unreleased work goes under ## [Unreleased]. Versions follow Semantic Versioning.
  • Inside a version, only these sections, in this order, and only those with entries: Added, Changed, Fixed, Security, Removed, Deprecated.
  • One line per entry: - **Area**: what the user can now do or will notice, in plain words. The area is a page or part the user knows (Canvas, Chat, Ready, To-do, Agents, Models, Tools, Memory, Knowledge, Triggers, Usage, Settings, CLIs, Install, Docs).
  • Say what changed for the user, not how it was built. No commit hashes or internal names. A breaking change starts with Breaking:.
  • A migration that changes saved data says so.
  • Link to the docs where a feature is explained.

items.title: Run from source
items.text: KOLONİ always runs from its source folder; Install covers that.

items.title: Live reload for the page (Windows)
items.text:
./scripts/dev.ps1

It starts the backend with KOLONI_DEV=1 and KOLONI_OPEN_BROWSER=0, and Vite's dev server on port 5173. Open the link the backend prints, with the port changed to 5173. KOLONI_DEV=1 lets the backend accept the page from port 5173. Stopping the script stops the backend too.

Vite sends /api to 127.0.0.1:8790, so run the dev backend on the default port.

items.title: After changing an API shape
items.text:
cd frontend
npm run generate:api

This writes frontend/src/api/generated.ts from the backend's schema. The full check fails while the committed file is stale.

items.title: Build this guide
items.text:
uv pip install -e ".[docs]"
zensical build      # the site in runtime/site
zensical serve      # or watch it at http://127.0.0.1:8000

.github/workflows/docs.yml builds the guide, checks it, and pushes it to the gh-pages branch under manual/, beside the site's root files in pages/, when started by hand, and on each push to main that changes the guide once the repository variable PAGES_ENABLED is true. Pages must be switched on once in the repository's Settings → Pages: Deploy from a branch, gh-pages, / (root) (.github/CI.md has the custom domain and DNS steps).

items.title: Licenses
items.text: KOLONİ, the whole project (backend and frontend), is licensed under the GNU Affero General Public License, version 3 or later (AGPL-3.0-or-later): see LICENSE and NOTICE in the repository. COMMERCIAL-LICENSE.md says what the AGPL asks and how to ask for a commercial license, and contributions come under the short CLA.md.

items.title: What KOLONİ includes
items.text:
THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md lists every third-party package KOLONİ ships, with its licence text: the page's bundled packages, its fonts (IBM Plex, under the SIL Open Font License), the Python packages, and other assets. It is generated by scripts/notices.py from pyproject.toml, frontend/package-lock.json and the installed packages; run it again after npm ci. Its last section lists the packages whose licences need a closer look.

Other included works:

  • The model catalogue (app/models_dev.json), trimmed from models.dev, under the MIT licence (app/models_dev.LICENSE).
  • The draw.io viewer (frontend/public/drawio/), unchanged, under the Apache License 2.0. KOLONİ's own script beside it keeps the viewer from loading anything from outside.

items.title: The full check
items.text:
cd frontend
npx playwright install chromium   # once
cd ..
./scripts/verify.ps1

verify.ps1 stops at the first step that fails. In order:

  1. pytest -q -n auto (in parallel);
  2. ruff check app tests scripts alembic;
  3. ty check app;
  4. in frontend/: the generated-API-types check, oxlint, the type check, the complexity check, Vitest, the build, the guide's checks (below; skipped when Zensical is not installed), and the Playwright end-to-end tests.

-BackendOnly runs only the first three. On Linux and macOS, run the script with pwsh; on Linux, install Playwright's browser with --with-deps.

The parallel test run can load a machine heavily. PYTEST_XDIST_AUTO_NUM_WORKERS sets how many processes -n auto starts.

items.title: Complexity
items.text:
No function may be more complex than 12 (McCabe: 1 plus each branch, loop, case, catch, ?:, &&, || and ??). Python's gate is ruff's C901 in the ruff step: a failure names the function and its value (is too complex (14 > 12)). The frontend's is npm run check:complexity (frontend/scripts/complexity.mjs), which fails when a function not in frontend/complexity-baseline.json is over 12, or a baselined one went up; each line gives the file, line, key (file::Outer>name) and value. Split the function; don't raise the limit.

Functions that were already over 12 when the gates came in are debt: a # noqa: C901 on the def line in Python, an entry in the baseline in the frontend. Both lists only shrink. When a function drops under 12, delete its noqa; the frontend check says you can lower or remove N baseline entries, and npm run check:complexity -- --update rewrites the baseline, lowering or dropping entries, never adding one. Renaming a baselined function makes it look new: rename its key in the baseline by hand.

items.title: End-to-end tests
items.text:
The Playwright tests start their own KOLONİ and a scripted model server, never a real one. They run with one worker.

  • KOLONI_E2E_PORT sets the test KOLONİ's port (9480 by default).
  • FAKE_MODEL_PORT sets the scripted model server's port (8081 by default); a stand-in llama server uses the next port. Two runs at once need model ports at least 2 apart.

items.title: The guide's checks
items.text:
uv pip install -e ".[docs]"                       # Zensical, once
.venv/Scripts/python.exe scripts/check_docs.py    # --no-build: check runtime/site as it is

It builds the guide, then fails on a link to a missing page or #anchor, a link in README.md, SECURITY.md or CHANGELOG.md to a missing file, a file a diagram's "From:" line names that is gone, or a setting the guide's Settings and Every setting pages name that the app's Settings page does not show (exact text, ignoring case). CI runs it on each push, and the Pages workflow before it publishes the guide.

items.title: Refreshing the guide's pictures
items.text:
The guide's screenshots in docs/images/ and its short videos in docs/videos/ are taken from the real app by frontend/e2e/guide-shots.spec.ts, with the scripted model, in the light theme: pictures at 1280×800, videos at 1280×720. A video is Playwright's own WebM recording, with a JPEG poster beside it; a page shows it with a <video> tag. The spec is skipped in an ordinary run. To take them again, build first, then from frontend/:

npm run build
$env:KOLONI_SHOTS = '1'; $env:KOLONI_E2E_PORT = '9500'; $env:FAKE_MODEL_PORT = '9510'
npx playwright test e2e/guide-shots.spec.ts --workers=1

A picture or video whose text names a folder of your home fails its test, so neither shows your own paths. Look at each one before you commit it.

In a page, a video's src is written from the page's own file (../videos/team.webm in docs/agents/teams.md) and its poster from the built page, one folder deeper (../../videos/team.jpg): Zensical rewrites the first and not the second.

items.title: Tests against real things
items.text:
Tests marked live are left out of verify:

.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest tests/test_live.py -m live
.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest tests/test_docker_executor.py -m live

The first needs a model server on port 8080 and, for its CLI tests, signed-in claude, codex and qodercli. The second needs a Docker daemon and the alpine image.

items.title: CI
items.text:
Each push and pull request to main runs the same checks once, on Ubuntu with Python 3.12 (.github/workflows/pr-check.yml): pytest, ruff and ty, the API types, the frontend's lint, typecheck, complexity, unit tests and build, and the guide's checks. A change to the guide or the plans alone runs only the guide's checks, or nothing.

End-to-end tests, the backend on Windows and on Python 3.13 and 3.14, and the Docker image run in heavy.yml, by hand from the Actions tab, or weekly once the repository variable HEAVY_WEEKLY is true. The repository is private and its Actions minutes are counted; .github/CI.md has the table and the reasons.

items.title: The guide's diagrams
items.text:
Each picture in the guide is a draw.io file here, name.drawio, with the SVG the pages show beside it, name.svg. The .drawio is the source: change it, then draw the SVG again. Each diagram's footer names the code it was drawn from and the day it was checked against it.

File Shown in system-map.drawio Architecture concept-map.drawio Home, KOLONİ in 5 minutes turn.drawio Chat and canvas permissions.drawio Permission levels memory.drawio Memory models.drawio Providers teams.drawio Recipes and candidates night.drawio Triggers, Work while you're away security.drawio Security model message-flow.drawio Architecture data-model.drawio Architecture runner.drawio Architecture cli-modes.drawio Set up a CLI working-copy.drawio Working copies and Take in recipe-engine.drawio Recipes and candidates install-update.drawio Backup and update

items.title: Opening and editing
items.text:
• In KOLONİ: open this folder as a project and click a .drawio file in the Workspace. KOLONİ's own draw.io viewer draws it; it shows the diagram, it does not edit it.
  • To edit: draw.io desktop, or app.diagrams.net (File → Open from → Device).

Keep the files easy to diff and the SVGs plain:

  • Save uncompressed (draw.io: File → Properties, untick Compressed). The files are plain XML, one shape per line.
  • Keep labels plain text: no Formatted Text (html=1) and no word wrap (whiteSpace=wrap); break lines yourself. Plain labels become plain SVG text, which every viewer shows the same way.
  • Give every shape a place. A shape without one is placed by KOLONİ's viewer, not where you meant.
  • When the code a diagram rests on changes, change the diagram and its footer's date.

items.title: Drawing the SVG again
items.text:
Draw the SVG with KOLONİ's own viewer, so every picture is drawn the same way:

  • In the Workspace, open the diagram and press Save as SVG. The picture is written beside it, over the old one: docs/diagrams/memory.drawio gives docs/diagrams/memory.svg.
  • Or ask an agent with the Diagram pictures tool for it ("draw docs/diagrams/memory.drawio as an SVG").

Both run the vendored viewer (frontend/public/drawio/) in a browser that loads nothing from the network. draw.io's own File → Export as → SVG also works, but its SVG differs from KOLONİ's; don't mix the two.

items.title: Picking the best of several candidates
items.text:
Give one job to several agents, score each result, and keep the best. The ready recipe Evolve does this with three Coders.

  1. Set a measure command. Settings › This project › Checks and git › Measure command: a command whose last line of output is a number from 0 to 100, for example python measure.py. Higher is better.
  2. Make the recipe. Agents → Recipes: pick Evolve and press Copy it, or draw your own step whose Who is Candidates (the best one goes on). Choose how many (2 to 5), their models (Auto, the Lead picks, Same model or I pick each), and a Target score if you want one. With a loop, the step is tried again while the best score is below the target.
  3. Use it. On the canvas, Teams for this chat → Manual, pick a team and this recipe. Then write your message.
  4. Pick the winner. Each candidate works in its own copy and is scored. A card lists the scores and asks which candidate's work goes on. At Full auto the best score goes on by itself.
  5. Take it in on the Teams' work is ready card.

A new round's result replaces the kept one only if it scores higher.

See Recipes and candidates.

items.title: Adding an MCP server safely
items.text:
An MCP server runs with your rights on this machine. These steps add one while keeping its tools behind your cards.

  1. Add it. Tools → Add → A server, ready-made (or from its page, pasting its setup text). Check the command and its arguments. Put any token in a variable, not in the arguments: "Other programs on this machine can see the arguments of the command".
  2. Look inside first. For an npx or uvx server, open its row and use What does it do?. It reads the package without running it and lists what it may reach: files, programs, the network. "This is where to look, not a verdict."
  3. Read its tools. Press Read its tools. Keep First look for it in osv.dev's known-malware records ticked.
  4. Leave it watching for a while. Until you trust it, every call of its tools asks you on a card, at every level, and the card shows the tool's own description. Use it in a chat and read what it asks.
  5. Trust it with Trust this server once you are content. If the page warns that it updates itself, pin a version in its command; otherwise your trust covers future versions too.
  6. Choose per tool. Under When an agent calls it, keep Ask for anything that changes things, choose Runs without asking only for tools that just read, and Off for what you do not need. (At Full auto, Ask runs without asking.)
  7. Give it only to the roles that need it, under Roles that may use it. Every tool's description is sent at every model step.

KOLONİ takes trust back by itself when the command or its variables change, or a new reading finds new or changed tools.

See MCP servers and trust.

items.title: A job while you're away
items.text: Jobs that run while you are away, for an hour or the night, each in its own copy of the project, so nothing changes until you take it in.

items.title: Before you go
items.text:
1. In a chat with a folder, tell the Orchestrator you are going away and what to work on meanwhile. It proposes the jobs on a While you're away card. The jobs run at this chat's permission level and on its model: below Full auto, a command no rule covers waits for you.
  2. Press Change the list to edit the jobs and add what is kept out (files or folders no job may change), then Save the list. On the card itself, set when to stop: Stop at a time, or after an amount of money. With neither set, the jobs run until they are done: there is no default spend limit, only your monthly budget if you set one.
  3. If you want the Orchestrator to answer the safe questions for you, use Let the Orchestrator answer what it safely can on the card. It stays on for the project after the jobs. Otherwise every question waits for you.
  4. Press Start. The top bar shows which job runs, with Stop all.

Leave KOLONİ running: closing it ends the jobs.

items.title: When you're back
items.text:
1. KOLONİ opens on the report on the canvas: what was done, what waits for your word, what could not be done. The chat says the same in one line.
  2. For a job that waits for a command, a change, a web request or an agent to open, press Allow and go on or Refuse. For a question, Open its chat and answer there.
  3. Look at each job's changes (See the changes), then Take in the ones you want, or Take in all.
  4. Try again runs a job that could not be done, or was stopped, again as an ordinary turn.
  5. Proposed while you were away, not started lists jobs the agents thought of; Add to To-do keeps them.

See Work while you're away.

items.title: Teaching an expert
items.text:
An expert is a role that knows one topic from its sources, advises and reads only.

  1. Make the expert. Agents → New role → An expert. Fill in Knows with the topic, and its sources, one a line: a docs site's address, files or a folder in the project. Press Create expert. The role is named "topic expert".
  2. Let it learn. On the Knowledge page, the topic's card shows what learning may cost beside Learn. Set At most this much a learning (USD) and Learn with (the model that writes the guide) if you want, then press Learn. KOLONİ reads the pages and a model writes a short guide.
  3. Check what it learned. Open the card: Guide shows the guide, Pages what was read and skipped, and Not known yet what it could not answer. Press Try it and ask what an agent would.
  4. Give it more if needed: add sources on its Settings tab and press Learn more. Learning again reads only what changed.
  5. Use it. The Orchestrator opens the expert when a job needs the topic. Other roles can use the same knowledge too: on a role's Knowledge tab, switch it on as Map.

When the guide has no answer, an expert with Agents may search the web when it has no answer may search; below Full auto that asks you first. What it finds can be added to the guide on a card.

See Knowledge and experts.

items.title: A web app with a team
items.text:
A small web app, built by the ready Web app team, from the first message to Take in.

  1. Open a folder for the app (the folder button → Open a folder…). An empty folder is fine.
  2. Pick the team. On the canvas, Teams for this chat → Manual, then the Web app team with its default recipe. Or leave Orchestrator decides and let it pick.
  3. Choose a level. Keep Ask before changes the first time. The team works in a working copy, so your folder does not change until you take the work in.
  4. Write the message, for example: "A one-page to-do list app in plain HTML and JavaScript, with a test." With Plan first on, you approve a plan first.
  5. Watch the canvas. It draws the team as a frame with its steps and agents, their tools, commands and files. Answer the cards as they come; Ready on the rail counts what waits.
  6. Preview it. An agent can start a dev server and show the page; running servers are listed under Previews in the Workspace.
  7. Take it in. When the recipe ends, the Teams' work is ready card asks: Take in, Fix the findings (if reviewers left findings), or Ask for changes with what to change.
  8. Undo if needed. Undo these changes takes a turn's changes back, and names what it cannot take back.

See Teams and Ready and approval cards.
