items.title: KOLONİ in 5 minutes
items.text:
KOLONİ's words, each in two or three sentences, with a link to the page that goes deeper. The map shows how they hang together.

KOLONİ's words and how they hang together.

items.title: Where you work
items.text: Project A folder of yours that agents work in. Each project has its own settings, memory, knowledge and   To-do list. To only talk, with no files and no commands, choose No folder · a plain chat.   See Quick start. Chat One conversation with the Orchestrator, in a project. Each chat has its own permission level, and   other folders can join it, read only or read & write. While agents work, a new message waits in a   queue. See Chat and canvas. Turn Everything that happens for one message: the Orchestrator's answer, the agents it opened, their   tools, commands and changes. The canvas draws one turn at a time, from what really happened.   See Chat and canvas.

items.title: Who does the work
items.text: The Orchestrator (Lead) The agent you talk to in a chat. It does small jobs itself and hands separate parts to sub-agents.   Behind the scenes its role is named Lead. See Roles. Sub-agent An agent that the Orchestrator, or another agent, opens for one part of the work. It changes files   in its own working copy, not in your folder. Opening one can ask you first (Settings › This project ›   Asking and away › Opening a sub-agent). See Permission levels. Role What an agent is for: a description, instructions, the tools it may use and, if you like, its own   model. KOLONİ comes with roles such as Coder, Reviewer, Tester, Planner and Product owner, and you can   add your own on the Agents page. See Roles. Tier How strong you say a model is: fast, balanced or strongest, set for each model on the   Models page. A role or a job can ask for a tier instead of one model; a model with no tier is only   ever picked by name. See Tiers and Agents may use.

items.title: Working together
items.text: Team A named group of roles, set out in stages: Plan, Build, Check, and Write & keep up. KOLONİ comes with teams such as Web app, Backend / API, Docs and Quality. Teams for this chat on the canvas decides whether the Orchestrator picks teams, you pick them, or no teams are used. See Teams. Recipe The drawn steps of a piece of work: who does each step, what runs at once, where it loops back and how it ends. A team runs by a recipe, such as Feature, Bugfix or Evolve. See Recipes and candidates and the Recipe cookbook. Room Two to six agents working on one goal at the same time, in one working copy. They share the work out first, each file has one holder, and the room has a budget. Open one with Work together… under More. See Rooms. Discussion Several agents talking one question through in rounds, while nobody changes anything. An agent with the discuss tool starts it (the Orchestrator has it); you can join in or end it. See Discussions.

items.title: Your say
items.text: Working copy and Take in A sub-agent changes files in a copy of your project, outside your folder, so your folder does not   change until you say so. Its work comes back on a card: Take in or Discard. A team's recipe keeps   its work in one copy until you press Take in. See   Working copies and Take in. Ready for you (cards) A card is a box that waits for your answer, such as "Run this command?" or a file change. Everything   that waits is listed in the Ready for you panel (the pill in the top bar) and on the Ready   page. The card where a recipe's work ends is Teams' work is ready, with Take in,   Fix the findings and Ask for changes. See Ready and approval cards. Permission levels What agents may do without asking: Ask before changes, Auto-edit files or Full auto.   Each chat has its own. Harmful commands, secret files and files that steer agents ask at every level,   with a few exceptions for CLIs run with their own tools (Known limits).   See Permission levels.

items.title: What it remembers
items.text: Memory What a project remembers between chats: your preferences, the project's rules, facts you approved,   and notes agents wrote while they worked. Your preferences and rules reach every agent; a fact reaches   an agent whose task names its subject; notes are found only when an agent looks. See   Memory. Knowledge What agents can look things up in: a docs site, files, a repository or a topic, read once and turned   into a short guide. A role uses a knowledge only if you give it to the role. Memory is what the project   learned; knowledge is reading you hand to agents. See Knowledge and experts.

items.title: Work that starts by itself
items.text: To-do A project's tasks, in your order. Each task runs in a chat of its own, by hand or one after another;   agents can propose tasks, and you decide when a task is done. See To-do. Trigger Starts a turn by itself: by the clock, when files change, or on a request from outside. Nobody watches   that turn, so it may do only what the trigger allows; everything else is refused. For work while you are   away, the Orchestrator can also plan a list of jobs. See Triggers and   Work while you're away.

items.title: Install
items.text: KOLONİ runs from its source folder. You install a few tools once, then build and start it.

items.title: What you need
items.text:
• Python 3.12, 3.13 or 3.14, and uv, which installs KOLONİ's Python packages.
  • Node.js 24, to build the page.
  • Git on your PATH. KOLONİ uses it to merge an agent's changes with yours and to commit when you ask.
  • At least one model, any of:
    • a model server that speaks the OpenAI API and supports tool calls, for example llama.cpp's llama-server started with --jinja, or a hosted API. Other OpenAI-compatible servers (Ollama, …) should work but are not tested;
    • an Anthropic API key;
    • a CLI installed and signed in in your own terminal. KOLONİ never signs in for you.
CLI Command Sign in Claude Code claude claude auth login Codex codex codex login GitHub Copilot CLI copilot gh auth login, or a GitHub token, or a model server of your own Qoder qodercli Qoder's own sign-in agy agy agy's own sign-in

Using a CLI through KOLONİ counts against your plan with that vendor.

  • Docker is optional: to run agents' commands in a container, or to run KOLONİ itself in one.

items.title: How well each system is tested
items.text: System State Windows Used and tested every day, with the real CLIs. Linux The automatic tests run on every change. A clean install and daily use are less tested. There are no desktop notifications. macOS Not tested yet. Docker The image has been built and started; it is the newest and least tested way to run KOLONİ.

items.title: Install and start
items.text:
Get KOLONİ's source folder, open a terminal in it, and run:

Windows (PowerShell)macOS and Linux 
uv venv .venv --python 3.12
uv pip install --python .venv/Scripts/python.exe -r requirements-dev.lock
uv pip install --python .venv/Scripts/python.exe --no-deps -e .
npm --prefix frontend ci
npm --prefix frontend run build
.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m app.main

uv venv .venv --python 3.12
uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python -r requirements-dev.lock
uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python --no-deps -e .
npm --prefix frontend ci
npm --prefix frontend run build
.venv/bin/python -m app.main

The window prints one line:

KOLONİ is open at http://127.0.0.1:8790/#key=…

Started from a terminal, KOLONİ also opens the page in your browser. Set KOLONI_OPEN_BROWSER=0 to stop that.

The part after #key= is the page key. Every request from the page must carry it, so a program on your machine (such as a command an agent runs) cannot approve its own cards or change your settings. Each start makes a new key. An old tab or bookmark shows "Open KOLONİ from the link in its window"; paste the new link there.

Stop KOLONİ with Ctrl+C in its window. A model server you started from the Models page stops with it.

If you skip the build step, KOLONİ serves only its API and there is no page to open.

items.title: This guide inside KOLONİ
items.text:
KOLONİ serves this guide at http://127.0.0.1:8790/guide/, and the Learn more → links in its hints open it there. It works offline and matches the version you run. Build it once with the optional Zensical package:

Windows (PowerShell)macOS and Linux 
uv pip install --python .venv/Scripts/python.exe -r pyproject.toml --extra docs
.venv/Scripts/zensical build

uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python -r pyproject.toml --extra docs
.venv/bin/zensical build

Without it KOLONİ runs as usual, and /guide/ says how to build the guide. Once Zensical is installed, the update scripts rebuild the guide on each update.

items.title: Where your data goes
items.text: Your data goes in runtime/ inside the KOLONİ folder: the database, working copies, backups and logs. To keep it elsewhere, set KOLONI_RUNTIME_ROOT before you start. API keys are stored in plain text in that database, so keep the folder private.

items.title: Another port
items.text:
KOLONİ uses port 8790. To use another one, for example to run a second KOLONİ next to the first:

Windows (PowerShell)macOS and Linux 
$env:KOLONI_PORT = 8800; .venv/Scripts/python.exe -m app.main

KOLONI_PORT=8800 .venv/bin/python -m app.main

Give each KOLONİ its own KOLONI_RUNTIME_ROOT too: two of them must not share a database.

items.title: Update
items.text:
Stop KOLONİ first (Ctrl+C in its window). Then, in its folder:

Windows (PowerShell)macOS and Linux 
./scripts/update.ps1

./scripts/update.sh

The script refuses while you have uncommitted changes in KOLONİ's files, or while something answers on KOLONİ's port (KOLONI_PORT, 8790). Otherwise it backs up the database, pulls the new version, updates the packages and rebuilds the page, and this guide where Zensical is installed. It stops at the first step that fails. Start KOLONİ again; the database is upgraded as it starts. -DryRun (Windows) or --dry-run (macOS and Linux) prints the steps without running them.

items.title: Docker
items.text:
The image holds the page, the API and the database in one container. It is for API keys and model servers: no CLI is in it. (This is not the project setting that runs agents' commands in Docker.)

docker build -t koloni .
docker run -it --name koloni -p 127.0.0.1:8790:8790 \
  -v koloni-data:/data \
  -v "$HOME/code/my-app:/projects/my-app" \
  koloni
  • Keep 127.0.0.1: in -p. Without it, the page is open to your network.
  • The link with the page key is printed at the start; docker logs koloni shows it again.
  • Your data is in the koloni-data volume: the database, working copies and logs, with keys in plain text.
  • Your projects are the folders you mount under /projects. Open one with the folder button. The container runs as user koloni (uid 1000); on Linux, files it writes in a mounted folder belong to uid 1000.
  • A model server on your machine: add -e KOLONI_MODEL_BASE_URL=http://host.docker.internal:8080/v1. On Linux, also add --add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway, and start the model server on the docker0 address (for example --host 172.17.0.1), never on 0.0.0.0.
  • Another port: use the same number on both sides and in KOLONI_PORT, for example -e KOLONI_PORT=8800 -p 127.0.0.1:8800:8800.
  • To update: git pull, build the image again, remove the old container (docker rm -f koloni), and start a new one with the same koloni-data volume. The database is backed up and upgraded as KOLONİ starts.
  • Do not mount Docker's socket into the container: whoever has the socket has full control of your machine.

The image has no Node.js, npx or uv, so MCP servers started with npx or uvx do not run in it. Webhooks, which call KOLONİ from your machine, are refused by the image.

items.title: Settings from the environment
items.text:
KOLONİ does not read a .env file. Set these in the shell before you start it.

Variable Default Meaning KOLONI_PORT 8790 The port on 127.0.0.1. KOLONI_RUNTIME_ROOT runtime/ Where the database and working files live. KOLONI_OPEN_BROWSER 1 0 does not open the browser at the start. KOLONI_PAGE_KEY a new one each start A fixed page key. KOLONI_MODEL_BASE_URL http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1 First start only: the address of the "Local" provider. KOLONI_MODEL_ID the first model the server lists First start only: Local's default model. KOLONI_MODEL_API_KEY none First start only: Local's key. KOLONI_DETECT_CLI 1 First start only: add Claude Code, Qoder, Codex and agy (switched off) if they are installed. 0 skips this.

After the first start, change providers on the Models page; the first-start variables no longer change them. The full list is in Environment variables.

items.title: Quick start
items.text: From install to your first approved change, in five steps.

items.title: 1. Install and start
items.text:
Follow Install for your system. When KOLONİ starts, its window prints one line:

KOLONİ is open at http://127.0.0.1:8790/#key=…

Started from a terminal, KOLONİ also opens this page in your browser. If it does not, open the link from the window. Keep the window open while you use KOLONİ; Ctrl+C in it stops KOLONİ.

On first open, the canvas shows First steps: a provider, a folder, and your first message. The step you are on has a button that takes you where you do it.

items.title: 2. Add a model
items.text:
Press Add a provider (in First steps, or on the Models page). Fill in:

  • Name: any name you like.
  • Kind: OpenAI-compatible server, Anthropic API, or a CLI: Claude Code (CLI), Codex (CLI), GitHub Copilot CLI, Qoder (CLI) or agy (CLI).
  • For a server: its Address (a llama.cpp server is usually http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1) and an API key if it needs one.
  • For the Anthropic API: your API key and a Default model.
  • For a CLI: nothing more, as long as the CLI is installed and you signed in to it in your own terminal. KOLONİ never signs in for you. If the CLI is missing or not signed in, its card shows the command to install it or sign in.

Press Save, then Test to check that it answers.

The first provider on the Models page is the default. KOLONİ makes one called "Local" at the first start, for a model server on this machine. If you do not run one, open your new provider and press Make default.

If a CLI was installed when KOLONİ first started, you may find it on the Models page already.

items.title: 3. Choose a folder
items.text: Press the folder button at the top left and choose Open a folder…. Pick the project your agents should work in. To only talk, without files or commands, choose No folder · a plain chat.

items.title: 4. Write your first message
items.text:
Next to the message box, check the permission level. Keep Ask before changes for now: each file change and each command will wait for you. See Permission levels.

Write what you want done, for example "Add a README that explains how to run this project", and send it.

The chat shows the Orchestrator's answer and a row for each agent it opened. The canvas draws the turn: each agent as a box with its tools, commands and files.

items.title: 5. Approve a card
items.text:
When an agent wants to change a file, a card shows the change as a diff. Press Approve to write it, or Reject to turn it down. After it is written you can still Revert it.

A command asks with "Run this command?":

  • Run once runs it this time.
  • Always run … runs it, and keeps a rule so the same kind of command runs without a card in this chat.
  • Reject turns it down.

While something waits for you, the project's tab above the canvas turns orange, and Ready on the rail counts it, so you can do something else meanwhile.

  • Settings: the app's and the project's settings.

items.title: Why KOLONİ
items.text: An agent CLI on its own works in one terminal, one session at a time. KOLONİ puts the agents you already use, and the models you choose, in one place on your own machine, and shows you what they really did.

items.title: What it adds
items.text:
• Many agents, one chat. The Orchestrator hands parts of a job to other roles (Coder, Reviewer, Tester and more), each in its own working copy, so your folder changes only when you take the work in.
  • Any model you have. Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot CLI, Qoder and agy on your own plans, an API key, or a model server on your own machine, side by side. Each agent shows the provider and model it really ran on.
  • Evidence, not a story. The canvas draws every turn from the record: the agents, their tools, commands and the files they changed, with real diffs. A value KOLONİ does not know is shown as unknown.
  • You decide. Before anything risky, an agent asks you on a card. The permission level sets how much runs without asking.
  • Memory with sources. Facts rest on lines of files and are checked again each time; a fact whose source changed is not used until you look.
  • Work that goes on. Teams follow recipes, triggers start work by themselves, and jobs run in copies while you are away.
  • Local. KOLONİ listens on 127.0.0.1 only, keeps its data in a folder on your machine, and sends no telemetry.

items.title: What it is not
items.text:
• Not finished: 0.1.0 is the first release, an alpha, so expect rough edges. See Known limits.
  • Not a sandbox by itself. Below Full auto your cards are the wall; for more, run commands in Docker. See Security model.

items.title: Limits
items.text: Each provider's window has a Limits tab. What it offers depends on how the provider is paid.

items.title: A CLI on a subscription
items.text: Step down a tier at [ ] % of the plan: once this much of the plan is used, agents picked by tier move one tier down. A whole number from 50 to 100, or empty for never. "A role that always runs on one tier, or on one model, is never stepped down: your own rule wins."

items.title: An API key
items.text:
• This key is a plan: count no money: its runs show no cost on Usage and count nothing in a project's budget.
  • Otherwise, At most $ … a day and At most $ … a month, spent at your prices, in every project. Empty means no limit. Past the limit, a new message whose Orchestrator runs on this provider asks you first, a model picked by tier moves to the next one of its tier, and no sub-agent or room member is opened here.

Press Save limits to keep them.

items.title: A model server on this machine
items.text: "A model server on this machine spends no money and has no plan: there is nothing to limit."

items.title: When a message would go over a limit
items.text: When a provider's limit or the project's monthly budget is reached, a new message asks first. It says which limit and how much was spent, then "Send it anyway?". Press Go on anyway to send it, or Cancel.

items.title: When an agent would move to a paid provider
items.text:
If KOLONİ would open a sub-agent on a provider that is paid per token, while the chat runs on one that is not, it asks on the Open this sub-agent? card. The card's reason says that the new provider is paid per token and the other is not. Press Open agent or Reject. Your answer counts for that provider for the rest of the turn. In a turn nobody watches, such an agent is not opened.

See also Usage and budgets.

items.title: Providers
items.text:
A provider is where your agents' models run. Open Models on the left rail to see them. Each provider is a card that shows how it is paid for (subscription for a CLI, this machine for a server on your own computer, API key otherwise) and what it has left. A click on a card opens its window.

The Models page with one provider, a model server on this machine.

items.title: Kinds of provider
items.text: Kind What it is OpenAI-compatible server A server that speaks the OpenAI API and supports tool calls, such as llama.cpp's llama-server or a hosted API. Other OpenAI-compatible servers (Ollama, …) should work but are not tested. Anthropic API Anthropic's API, with your key. Claude Code (CLI), Codex (CLI), GitHub Copilot CLI, Qoder (CLI), agy (CLI) A CLI on this machine that you are signed in to. It runs on your plan with that vendor.

items.title: Adding a provider
items.text:
Press Add a provider ("A CLI with your subscription, an API key, or a server of your own"). Give it a Name and a Kind, then:

  • For a server: its Address and, if it needs one, an API key. "Keys are kept in plain text in KOLONİ's local database on this machine."
  • For the Anthropic API: an API key and a Default model.
  • For a CLI: Path to the command, if it is not found by its name. KOLONİ never signs in for you. If the CLI is missing or not signed in, the window shows the command to install it or to sign in, with links to the vendor's docs.

Press Add provider to save it.

items.title: The provider window
items.text:
The window has the tabs Models, Connection and Limits. A server on this machine also has Server.

Connection holds what you filled in when you added it, and:

  • Default model: the model used when nothing else names one.
  • At most this many agents at once: how many agents may run on this provider at the same time.
  • How it runs (CLIs only):
Option What it means One session per agent, with KOLONİ's tools (recommended) One CLI session per agent, using KOLONİ's tools and cards. One run per model step, with KOLONİ's tools The CLI runs once per model step: slower, and the answer arrives all at once. Native: its own tools, in the project The CLI uses its own tools in your folder, and asks KOLONİ before each one. Reads with its own tools; started without leave to write or run agy only: it reads, and cannot change anything.
  • Sign-in (Claude Code and Codex): My own uses the sign-in in your home folder; Its own for KOLONİ keeps a separate one, and the window shows the command to log in to it. "KOLONİ never sees the token."

The buttons at the bottom:

  • Save saves the changes.
  • Test checks the provider. For a CLI it only says whether the command was found: "It was not run, so sign-in is not checked." For the Anthropic API it asks for the model's details, which spends nothing. For an OpenAI-compatible server it sends one small request ("Call the ping tool.") to see whether the model can use tools; on a paid service that costs a few tokens. It then says "Reachable" and the model.
  • Try a real run (CLIs): runs the CLI once on a one-word question. This counts against your plan.
  • Make default: makes this provider the default, the first one in the list.
  • Remove key: shown when a key is saved.
  • Delete provider: deletes it at once, without asking. The last provider cannot be deleted ("At least one provider is needed"). Chats and roles that used it go back to having no choice.

items.title: Switching a provider off
items.text: Each provider has an on / off switch, on its card and at the top of its window. "Off: nothing new starts on it - no chat, no agent, no learning; its key and settings stay. A turn already running goes on until it ends; Stop ends it now." Its card then says "switched off".

items.title: The models of a provider
items.text:
The Models tab lists the models that agents and you can pick, at most 30. Each row has:

Column What it does Tier How strong the model is: fast, balanced or strongest. See Tiers. Context, Max output, Thinking What the model can take in, write out, and its thinking levels. Price in / out (1M) The price per million tokens; "plan" for a CLI. Agents may use On: agents may pick this model by themselves. Off: only you pick it. On Off: the model is not used.

Open a row for more, such as Its note for agents (what the model is for, up to 120 characters) and Used in 30 days. Each change saves at once.

Add a model adds one by name. Fill from the catalogue proposes a list: your rows first, then what the provider lists with your key, then the bundled models.dev catalogue's models, with their details; nothing changes until you press Save these models. At the top of the page, Update catalogue downloads a newer catalogue, and Keep the catalogue fresh lets KOLONİ do that by itself.

items.title: Which model a chat uses
items.text:
The model button under the message box opens Model for this conversation: a Provider (the first option is the default) and a Model name. Use this model applies it from the next turn. "A role with its own model keeps it."

An agent's model is chosen in this order:

  1. the models the role lists under Try first, in your order, unless the agent that opens it gave the job a tier;
  2. the role's own model (One model);
  3. the first model of the role's tier, or of the tier the opener gave the job;
  4. the chat's model;
  5. the default provider, the first one in the list.

A model past its limit, down, switched off or not one agents may use is passed over, and the next is tried. Roles and their models are set on the Agents page.

Where an agent runs: the full order, tiers, limits and moves. See also Tiers and Limits.

items.title: Plan meters
items.text: For Claude Code, Codex, agy and Copilot, the top bar shows how much of the plan is used, from what each CLI last reported. Click a meter to open Usage. On a provider's card, Read now reads the plan again; for Claude Code that is one short request.

items.title: A model server on this machine: the Server tab
items.text: For an OpenAI-compatible server on this machine, the Server tab starts and stops your llama.cpp llama-server. Set Program to the full path of llama-server in your llama.cpp build (the one on PATH is filled in when there is one), choose the Model from the models folder next to it, set the context, GPU layers and the other values, then press Start. Server output shows what the server prints. "It starts only when you press Start, and stops when KOLONİ closes. No agent can start it; Start runs exactly what is shown here."

items.title: Set up an API provider
items.text: An API provider is a service you pay per token, with a key: the Anthropic API, or any service that speaks the OpenAI API.

items.title: Anthropic API
items.text:
1. Models → Add a provider. Kind: Anthropic API.
  2. API key: your Anthropic key. "Keys are kept in plain text in KOLONİ's local database on this machine." Once saved, the key "is never shown again".
  3. Address: leave it empty for https://api.anthropic.com.
  4. Default model: needed, for example claude-sonnet-5-5.
  5. Workspace ID: "Only needed for a key that is not scoped to a workspace. Copy it from the Anthropic console."
  6. Press Add provider, then Test. For the Anthropic API, Test reads the model's details and spends nothing.

items.title: A service that speaks the OpenAI API
items.text:
1. Models → Add a provider. Kind: OpenAI-compatible server.
  2. Address: the service's API address, starting with http:// or https://. The field suggests the services KOLONİ knows from its model catalogue; an address that only names a known service is completed to its full API address.
  3. API key: the service's key. The field says what the service calls its key.
  4. Default model: if you leave it empty, KOLONİ uses the first model the server lists.
  5. Press Add provider, then Test. Test sends one small request to see whether the model can use tools, which costs a few tokens on a paid service. It then says "Reachable" and the model, and adds "this model does not take tools" if it cannot use them.

A model that does not take tools can chat, but agents cannot use KOLONİ's tools with it.

items.title: After adding
items.text:
• At most this many agents at once: 8 by default for a service.
  • On the Models tab, give the models a Tier, and set Agents may use. See Tiers and Agents may use.
  • On the Limits tab, set dollars a day or a month, or mark the key as a plan. See Limits.
  • Prices come from the catalogue unless you set your own. See Usage and budgets.

items.title: Set up a CLI
items.text: A CLI provider runs an agent CLI that you installed and signed in to yourself: Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot CLI, Qoder or agy. It runs on your plan with that vendor. KOLONİ never installs a CLI and never signs in for you. Read Subscription rules first.

items.title: Steps
items.text:
1. Install the CLI in your own terminal. If it is missing, the provider's window shows the install command for your system, with a link to the vendor's install docs.
  2. Sign in in your own terminal (see the table). If it is not signed in, the window shows the sign-in command.
  3. Models → Add a provider, and pick its Kind. Set Path to the command only if KOLONİ does not find it by its name.
  4. Choose How it runs (see below), and press Add provider.
  5. Test only checks that the command is found; it does not run it. Try a real run runs it once on a one-word question, on your plan.

At the first start, KOLONİ adds Claude Code, Qoder, Codex and agy by itself if they are installed. It never adds Copilot by itself. It adds agy switched off: Google's terms forbid using Antigravity through another app (see Subscription rules). Its card on the Models page, switched on or off, says "Google's terms forbid using Antigravity through another app; your Google account may be suspended." KOLONİ adds providers only at the first start, so an agy already on the Models page is left as it is.

items.title: The CLIs
items.text: Kind Command Sign in Claude Code (CLI) claude claude auth login Codex (CLI) codex codex login GitHub Copilot CLI copilot gh auth login, or a GitHub token Qoder (CLI) qodercli Qoder's own sign-in agy (CLI) agy agy's own sign-in

items.title: How it runs
items.text:
CLI Choices (the first is the default) Claude Code One session per agent · One run per model step · Native Codex One session per agent · One run per model step · Native. As a session its own patch tool cannot be switched off: KOLONİ refuses every patch it asks to make, and it writes with KOLONİ's write_file and edit_file instead. Unlike Native, it runs wherever the other sessions run: triggers, To-do, While you're away, recipe steps and comparisons. The default since 7 Nov 2026; a Codex provider added before keeps the way it was saved with. One added with a model server of your own starts as One run per model step, since its session there is not yet measured. Copilot One session per agent · Native Qoder One session per agent · Native. Set a model name if Qoder's own default model does not answer. agy Reads with its own tools · Native
  • One session per agent and One run per model step use KOLONİ's tools and cards, with the CLI's own tools off.
  • Native uses the CLI's own tools in your folder. Claude Code, Qoder and agy ask KOLONİ before every tool they use; Codex before each command and patch, except the commands its own rules count as safe, which it runs without asking; Copilot before each command, write and read.
  • Reads with its own tools (agy): it reads, and is started without leave to write or run.

A trigger never starts a CLI that works with its own tools (Native, or agy's reads): with nobody watching, only an agent that works with KOLONİ's tools runs.

The modes, KOLONİ's tool bridge, and how each CLI asks. (full size)

items.title: Going on from the last turn
items.text:
Only Claude Code, run Native with Sign-in: Its own for KOLONİ, goes on in its own session from one turn to the next: it is sent only what is new, and compacts that session itself. Every other CLI lead starts each turn anew and is sent the whole chat. KOLONİ compacts that, as it does for an API model, past Summarise a long context at (%) of the window set on its role; with no window set there, only Compact now compacts it. A CLI run One run per model step is never compacted: each step is sent a trimmed history.

Compact now is in the top bar's context button (see Chat and canvas).

items.title: Qoder's free models
items.text: Qoder puts a free model's request in a queue when it is busy. In tests the wait was about 1 to 3 minutes, once longer. While it waits, the agent's window says so, for example "Qoder: in the model's queue for 2 min 43 s (waits up to 60 min)", and its box on the canvas says "queued 2 min". A sub-agent still queued after 90 seconds is moved to the next model of its tier, where KOLONİ picked its model and the tier has another; a move that may cost money is asked on a card first (see Ready and approval cards). In a turn you watch, a lead, or a sub-agent that cannot be moved, waits as long as Qoder keeps it queued; in a trigger's or a job's turn while you're away it gives up after 90 seconds. Run Native, Qoder shows no queue line, and is not moved.

items.title: Sign-in for Claude Code and Codex
items.text:
Sign-in offers My own (the sign-in in your home folder) or Its own for KOLONİ: a sign-in folder for this provider alone, so that several accounts can run side by side. For its own, save the provider, then the window gives the command to log in to it in your own terminal. "KOLONİ never sees the token."

Claude Code and Codex can also Use a model server of your own instead (optional): a Model server address on this machine or your network.

items.title: GitHub Copilot CLI
items.text:
• API key: leave it empty to use your own GitHub sign-in (gh), or give a fine-grained GitHub token with the Copilot Requests permission. A token has not been tried on a real account yet.
  • Thinking: KOLONİ sends Copilot's levels Off to Max (Off as none), whether it runs as a session or Native; the Models page shows "Off–Max". A level the model does not take gives no error.
  • Model auto: Copilot picks the model for each request. It is in Copilot's model list (tier fast) and takes no thinking level, so KOLONİ sends none. Pick a model for Copilot, auto or another: with no model and Medium thinking, Copilot's default spent 7.12 AI credits for the same short answer that auto answered for 0.18 (measured once, 7 Nov 2026, Copilot CLI 1.0.105). The agent's node and window show the model auto picked (auto → gpt-6-luna), and its Details say why; an agent that goes on from it asks for auto again.
  • Usage: Copilot's tokens and AI credits (or premium requests) are counted from its usage checkpoint, run as a session as in Native. As a session that was measured with copilot -p (CLI 1.0.103), not yet seen in a live session. See Usage and budgets.
  • Copilot can also use a model server of your own, with Server type, Most prompt tokens and Most output tokens. Never connect to GitHub then means no sign-in, telemetry or update check, and web tools are off.

items.title: Plan meters
items.text:
For Claude Code, Codex, agy and Copilot, the provider's card shows what is left of the plan, and Read now reads it again (for Claude Code, one short request). For Claude Code, the Limits tab also offers Keep it fresh from your Claude Code sessions: a status line you add to your own Claude Code settings, so that your sessions report what is left of your plan.

See CLIs for what has been measured.

items.title: Set up a local model
items.text: A model on your own machine spends no money and sends nothing out. KOLONİ talks to it through the OpenAI API, so the model server must support tool calls.

items.title: llama.cpp
items.text:
KOLONİ is built and tested with llama.cpp's llama-server. Start it with --jinja, so that tool calls work. Its usual address is http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1.

At the first start, KOLONİ makes a provider called "Local" at that address (or at KOLONI_MODEL_BASE_URL). It counts as set up only while its server answers.

items.title: Starting the server from KOLONİ
items.text:
For an OpenAI-compatible provider whose address is on this machine, the provider's window has a Server tab:

  • Program: your llama-server program.
  • Model: a model file, or none.
  • Context (-c), GPU layers (-ngl), Default thinking, Temperature, Top-p, Top-k, Min-p.
  • Advanced: every other argument, as given.

The tab's first values are only a starting point: the llama-server on your PATH (if there is none, set Program to its full path), --port 8080 --jinja, and no model. For your own build, set Program to the full path of llama-server in its bin folder. Model lists the .gguf files in the models folder next to that program. KOLONİ keeps the tab's values when you press Start or Restart, in local-server.json under runtime/; until then, KOLONI_LOCAL_SERVER can name the program (see Environment variables).

Check the values for your machine, then press Start. The tab shows whether it runs, the GPU's memory and load (from nvidia-smi), and Server output. "It starts only when you press Start, and stops when KOLONİ closes. No agent can start it; Start runs exactly what is shown here."

At most this many agents at once: for a server on this machine, KOLONİ reads the server's slots when its first agent starts.

items.title: Other model servers
items.text: Any server that speaks the OpenAI API and supports tool calls can be added the same way: Models → Add a provider → OpenAI-compatible server, with its address. Such servers (Ollama, …) should work but are not tested: the local server KOLONİ is measured with is llama.cpp's llama-server. KOLONİ has no settings of its own for those servers, and the Server tab starts only llama-server. Press Test to see whether the model can use tools.

items.title: After adding
items.text:
• Give the models a Tier and set Agents may use on the Models tab. See Tiers and Agents may use.
  • "A model server on this machine spends no money and has no plan: there is nothing to limit."
  • If the model takes long to load, raise KOLONI_MODEL_FIRST_TOKEN_SECONDS. See Environment variables.

items.title: Subscription rules
items.text: When you use a CLI through KOLONİ, you use your own subscription with that vendor. Each vendor has its own terms for that. This page says what each vendor's official page says, as read on 5 November 2026. It is not legal advice: read the terms yourself, and decide.

items.title: What KOLONİ does
items.text: KOLONİ starts the CLI that you installed and signed in to yourself, unchanged, and sends it prompts. It does not read the CLI's sign-in token, and it does not talk to the vendor's service for the CLI. For Claude Code, you can have KOLONİ keep a separate sign-in folder; you still sign in through Anthropic's own sign-in.

items.title: What each vendor's page says
items.text: Vendor Its page What it says Anthropic (Claude Code) Legal and compliance Third-party developers may not offer a Claude.ai sign-in in their own apps, or collect, store or route users' credentials or session tokens. The exception is an end user signing in to the unchanged Claude Code program with their own subscription. The page does not speak of another app starting the CLI. OpenAI (Codex) Authentication The page could not be read in full. For apps, the official way is "Sign in with ChatGPT" (preview). No text was found that allows or forbids another program using Codex's own ChatGPT sign-in. GitHub (Copilot CLI) Use Copilot CLI It documents running the CLI from scripts and with -p. It says nothing against another tool running it. Requests count as premium requests (Copilot requests). Copilot's own terms were not read. Google (Antigravity, agy) Terms, section 6 "Using third party software, tools, or services to access the Service (e.g. using OpenClaw with Antigravity OAuth) is a breach of this Agreement." It warns that Antigravity and Gemini CLI accounts can be suspended. Qoder Terms of Service (29 April 2026), Run in scripts The docs endorse headless use (-p) in "Shell scripts, automation workflows, and CI/CD Pipelines". The terms forbid sharing your account or letting a third party use it (2.3), and scraping outputs with scripts (3.2.10). Nothing forbids a local tool starting the CLI under your own sign-in. No page states limits for the free models.

items.title: Open questions
items.text:
agy: switched off

Whether KOLONİ starting agy counts as "third party software … to access the Service" is not settled, but it is close to the example Google gives. So KOLONİ adds agy switched off, and its card on the Models page says why. Switching it on is your choice, and your risk with your Google account.

  • Codex: no rule either way was found.
  • Qoder: allowed for your own use as far as the pages say; your sign-in or access token is never given to anyone else.

What a CLI's use costs you is set by your plan; see Usage and budgets.

items.title: Tiers
items.text:
A tier is how strong you say a model is: fast, balanced or strongest. You set it in the Tier column of a provider's Models tab. Fill tiers fills them from the catalogue.

Tiers let KOLONİ pick a model for a job instead of one fixed name:

  • a role can ask for a tier instead of one model;
  • an agent can call a job easy or hard, to go one tier down or up;
  • a chat's Orchestrator can follow how hard your message is.

A model with no tier is only ever picked by name.

items.title: The tier lists
items.text:
Below the provider cards, the Models page shows three lists: Strongest, Balanced and Fast. Each lists its models, numbered in the order they are tried. Drag a model, or use its move up and move down buttons, to change the order; each move saves at once. A model that agents may not use is marked "off for agents". With no tiers at all, the page says "No model has a tier yet".

A model greyed with its provider's state ("not answering") shows how that provider looked when the page read it. A provider that is not installed, not signed in or without a key is passed over until KOLONİ sees it again: the page reads it, or you press its Check. A model server is passed over after not answering for two minutes. Where every model of a tier looks so, the first is still tried.

items.title: Agents may use
items.text:
Each model has an Agents may use switch. On, agents may pick the model by themselves, for example by its tier. Off, only you pick it: in a chat's model picker, or as a role's own model.

A provider with no list of models has one switch for the whole provider: Agents may use this provider. Never run a model that is not on this list keeps agents to the listed models.

What it is good for (for a provider) and Its note for agents (for a model) are short notes that agents read when they choose.

items.title: A role's model
items.text: On the Agents page each role chooses who picks its model: Orchestrator, As the chat, One tier (Fast, Balanced or Strongest) or One model. See Roles.

items.title: Orchestrator model: automatic
items.text: In the chat's model picker, Orchestrator model: automatic sends each message to a fast model, which judges it easy, normal or hard. The Orchestrator then runs on a fast, balanced or strongest model. That is one more request for each message you send. It overrides the Orchestrator role's own model and tier. A trigger's message does not use it.

items.title: What spends extra requests
items.text:
Some settings make one more model request each time. Each says so where you switch it on.

What When it spends Note what the work found, by itself (Settings › This project › Memory and web) One request after every message. Have a model look over each sub-agent's report (Settings › This project › Agents) One request after every sub-agent's report. Orchestrator model: automatic (the chat's model picker) One request for each message you send. The Orchestrator answers what it safely can (Settings › This project › Asking and away › When you're away), on a CLI One request of your plan for each answer. Try a real run (Models page, a CLI) One short run, on your plan. Read now for Claude Code (a provider's card) One short request. Search by meaning (Memory page) One embeddings request for each search. Learning a knowledge topic (Knowledge page) Model requests, up to the limit you set. Candidates in a recipe Each candidate is its own agent. Agents on a CLI working at the same time They spend your subscription at the same time.

items.title: Ways to keep a job cheap
items.text:
• Give models tiers, and let roles ask for a tier, so easy jobs go to a fast model. See Tiers.
  • Turn off Agents may use for an expensive model you want to pick only by hand.
  • Set a Monthly budget and a token limit per message (Settings › This project › Limits and money), and dollar limits on API keys (a provider's Limits tab).
  • Keep Agents at the same time and Sub-agents per request low (Settings › This project › Limits and money).
  • Give an MCP server only to the roles that need it, and switch off tools you do not use: every tool's description is sent at every model step.
  • Use a model server on your own machine for work that does not need a large model: it spends no money.
  • On GitHub Copilot CLI, give the provider a model. Copilot's auto picks one for each request; with no model and Medium thinking, Copilot's default spent 7.12 AI credits for the same short answer that auto answered for 0.18 (measured once, 7 Nov 2026, Copilot CLI 1.0.105). See GitHub Copilot CLI.

See Usage and budgets.

items.title: The Usage page
items.text:
Open Usage on the left rail. Choose This project or All projects, and a period: Today, 7 days, 30 days or All.

The Usage page, counted from the record: no model is asked.

At the top: Messages, Tokens sent, Tokens written and Cost. Below:

  • By provider and model: messages, agents, tokens and cost for each model.
  • By conversation.
  • Who started it: You, A trigger, with nobody watching, or KOLONİ itself (requests KOLONİ makes outside a message, such as a real run of a CLI from the Models page).

"Nothing is estimated": tokens are only what the models reported, and what was not reported shows as "–".

GitHub Copilot CLI reports what it spent in its usage checkpoint: its tokens, and its own unit, AI credits (or premium requests, its older unit). They show on the agent's context line, under Details in its window, such as "1,200 in / 300 out · 0.42 AI credits". Run as a session, they are counted from that checkpoint as in Native: measured with copilot -p (CLI 1.0.103), not yet seen in a live session.

items.title: Where the money comes from
items.text:
KOLONİ shows money only from prices:

  1. your own price for a model, if you set one;
  2. otherwise the price in the bundled models.dev catalogue, in USD.

A CLI on a plan has no price for a token, so it never has a cost here. Neither does an API key marked This key is a plan: count no money. A cost shown with "≥" means part of it has no price. Amounts in different currencies are never added together.

items.title: Prices
items.text: The Prices fold lists the models and their prices per million tokens sent and written, and optionally for cache reads and writes. Type a price and a currency, then Save price. "A price belongs to the model's name, whichever provider runs it." Use models.dev's goes back to the catalogue's price.

items.title: A project's monthly budget
items.text:
Set it under Settings › This project › Limits and money › Monthly budget, in the currency of your prices (else USD). It covers this calendar month, by this machine's clock.

  • At 80%, KOLONİ tells you once, and the top bar shows it.
  • At 100%, a new message asks first: "Over this month's budget. Send it anyway?" Press Go on anyway or Cancel. Triggers start none.
  • Work on a model with no price is not counted.
  • If your prices are in more than one currency, the budget is not enforced, and the page says so.
  • A plain chat (no folder) belongs to no budget.

The Usage page shows This month's budget, how much is used, and Change in Settings →.

items.title: A limit per message
items.text: Settings › This project › Limits and money › Stop the work on a message over this many tokens. KOLONİ checks it before each model step and stops the work once a message's work goes over it.

items.title: Providers' own limits
items.text: Each provider can have a limit in dollars a day or a month, or step down a tier when a plan runs low. See Limits.

items.title: Plan meters
items.text: For Claude Code, Codex, agy and Copilot, the top bar shows how much of the plan is used, from what each CLI last reported. Near the limit (90%), KOLONİ tells you. On the Usage page, Plan limits shows the same with Check now: "These are the limits of the account the CLI on this machine is signed in to."

items.title: Before the start
items.text: Environment variables: see Environment variables.

items.title: CLIs
items.text:
What KOLONİ supports for each CLI. How to set one up is in Set up a CLI.

CLI Command How it runs (default first) Native asks KOLONİ before Plan read Versions measured with KOLONİ Claude Code claude session, step, native every tool it uses yes (one short request) 2.1.310, 2.1.311, 2.1.312 Codex codex session, step, native (step first on a model server of your own) each command and patch, but not those its own rules count as safe yes 0.163.0, 0.164.0 GitHub Copilot CLI copilot session, native each command, write and read yes 1.0.91, 1.0.103 Qoder qodercli session, native every tool it uses (not yet measured) no — agy agy reads, native every tool it uses yes 1.3.3, 1.4.7, 1.4.8

items.title: A version that was not measured
items.text: KOLONİ records which versions of each CLI it was measured with. A newer version is never refused. KOLONİ tries it once; if it answers as expected it runs, with a note that this version was not measured with KOLONİ. If not, it runs the old way: with KOLONİ's tools, and the CLI's own tools off.

items.title: What every CLI has in common
items.text:
• You install it and sign in yourself, in your own terminal.
  • Its use counts against your plan with that vendor; KOLONİ shows no money for it.
  • Triggers do not start a CLI that works with its own tools.
  • When a CLI runs Native, its model reads its commands' raw output; KOLONİ masks keys only in what it records and shows.

See Subscription rules and Known limits.

items.title: Environment variables
items.text:
KOLONİ reads these when it starts. It does not read a .env file: set them in the shell before you start it.

Windows (PowerShell)macOS and Linux 
$env:KOLONI_PORT = 8800; .venv/Scripts/python.exe -m app.main

KOLONI_PORT=8800 .venv/bin/python -m app.main

items.title: Where and how KOLONİ runs
items.text: Variable Default What it does KOLONI_PORT 8790 The port KOLONİ listens on. KOLONI_RUNTIME_ROOT runtime/ in KOLONİ's folder Where the database, working copies, backups and logs are kept. Two KOLONİs must not share one. KOLONI_HOST 127.0.0.1 The address KOLONİ listens on. Anything other than 127.0.0.1, ::1 or localhost is refused at the start, except inside the Docker image. KOLONI_PAGE_KEY a new one each start A fixed page key. KOLONİ takes it out of its own environment once read, so its commands and agents do not get it. KOLONI_OPEN_BROWSER 1 0: do not open the page in the browser at the start. KOLONI_DEV not set 1: also accept the live-reload page on port 5173 (for development).

items.title: The first start only
items.text:
These make the first providers. After the first start, change providers on the Models page; changing these does nothing to providers that already exist.

Variable Default What it does KOLONI_MODEL_BASE_URL http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1 The address of the "Local" provider. KOLONI_MODEL_ID the first model the server lists Local's default model. KOLONI_MODEL_API_KEY none Local's key. KOLONI_DETECT_CLI 1 First start only: add Claude Code, Qoder, Codex and agy (switched off) as providers if they are installed. 0 skips this.

items.title: Models and agents
items.text: Variable Default What it does KOLONI_MODEL_FIRST_TOKEN_SECONDS 900 How long a model may take to start answering before the run fails. KOLONI_MODEL_STALL_SECONDS 120 How long an answer may pause before the run fails. KOLONI_CONTEXT_CHARS 240000 How much history, in characters, an agent keeps when its model's context window is not known. KOLONI_SEARCH_SECONDS 20 How long a search through the project's files may take before it is given up. A value that is not a positive number is ignored.

items.title: Background work
items.text: Variable Default What it does KOLONI_TRIGGER_CLOCK 1 0: triggers do not start by themselves. KOLONI_CATALOGUE_REFRESH 1 0: never download the model catalogue at the start. Otherwise it is downloaded again once it is a week old, unless Keep the catalogue fresh is off on the Models page.

items.title: The local model server and MCP servers
items.text: Variable Default What it does KOLONI_LOCAL_SERVER llama-server on PATH The program the Models page's Server tab starts, until you choose another there: the full path of llama-server in a llama.cpp build's bin folder. KOLONI_NVIDIA_SMI nvidia-smi The program the Server tab asks for GPU memory and load. KOLONI_MCP_HOME KOLONI/mcp/ in your cache folder (%LOCALAPPDATA% on Windows), one folder per runtime Where the MCP servers KOLONİ starts keep their files.

items.title: Variables KOLONİ gives to commands
items.text: Agents' commands get this machine's environment, except variables with secret names (such as GITHUB_TOKEN or OPENAI_API_KEY) and the ways into a program you are signed in to (GIT_ASKPASS, SSH_AUTH_SOCK, VSCODE_*, CLAUDE_CODE_* and the like), unless you name them under Settings › This project › Commands and secrets › Secret variables commands may see. A project whose tests use git over ssh needs SSH_AUTH_SOCK named there. KOLONİ's own git, which pushes for you, keeps all of them. With Planted test key (canary) on, they also get a made-up KOLONI_CANARY_KEY. In Docker, commands get none of this machine's environment.

items.title: KOLONİ's own data: runtime/
items.text:
In KOLONİ's folder, or wherever KOLONI_RUNTIME_ROOT says.

Path What it holds data/koloni.db The database. API keys are in it, in plain text. data/backups/ Copies of the database made before upgrades and by the update script (the last five). logs/koloni.log The log; it rotates at 10 MB and keeps five old files. attachments/ Files attached to messages, per chat. skills/ KOLONİ's copies of skills. copies/ Sub-agents' working copies (see below). cli-homes/ Claude Code's and Codex's sign-in folders, one per provider, when you chose Its own for KOLONİ. Kept across restarts. server-homes/ Empty settings folders for Claude Code and Codex when they run on a model server of your own, with none of your sign-in. agy-home/ A new folder for each agy run, cleared when KOLONİ starts. models_dev.json The model catalogue, once updated. local-server.json The Server tab's settings. before-restore/ Your data as it was before a restore. Never removed by KOLONİ.

runtime/ is in .gitignore.

items.title: Outside runtime/
items.text:
• Working copies: if runtime/copies would be inside a git repository (as it is in KOLONİ's own folder), copies go to %LOCALAPPDATA%\KOLONI\copies on Windows, or ~/.local/share/KOLONI/copies elsewhere.
  • GitHub Copilot CLI gets an empty settings folder inside each run's temporary folder, removed when the run ends. It signs in with the provider's token, or else with your own gh login.
  • Qoder uses your own sign-in and settings folder (~/.qoder); KOLONİ gives it no folder of its own.
  • Claude Code and Codex with My own sign-in use yours (~/.claude, ~/.codex).
  • MCP servers start in %LOCALAPPDATA%\KOLONI\mcp on Windows, ~/Library/Caches/KOLONI/mcp on macOS, or ~/.cache/KOLONI/mcp on Linux.

items.title: In your project
items.text: KOLONİ's own files are under .koloni/; see Recipe, role and skill formats. KOLONİ never changes your project's own .gitignore. Files you save from a message go to docs/attachments/.

items.title: What an export holds
items.text: Export everything holds the database, skills/, attachments/, models_dev.json and local-server.json. It does not hold your projects, their .koloni/, working copies, logs, CLI sign-ins or the database backups. See Backup and update.

items.title: Recipes
items.text:
A recipe kept in a folder is a JSON file in .koloni/recipes/, named from the recipe in lowercase ASCII with hyphens. KOLONİ writes it when you save from the Recipes tab; you can also read or change it by hand. A file KOLONİ cannot read is listed with the reason.

{
  "name": "Bugfix",
  "graph": {
    "version": 1,
    "steps": [
      { "id": "fix", "name": "Fix it", "who": { "role": "Coder" } },
      { "id": "test", "name": "Test it", "who": { "role": "Tester" }, "done_when": "no_findings" }
    ],
    "groups": [],
    "ends": [{ "id": "end", "then": "in" }],
    "arrows": [
      { "from": "start", "to": "fix" },
      { "from": "fix", "to": "test" },
      { "from": "test", "to": "end" }
    ],
    "loops": [{ "from": "test", "to": "fix", "rounds": 2 }]
  }
}
  • name: 1 to 60 characters.
  • Ids: letters, digits, _ and -, at most 40. start is the user's message.
  • steps (at most 60): id, name, who, and optionally done_when (done or no_findings), if_fails (ask or stop), ask_me (true or false), group (a group's id), when ("problem": only if the step before found a problem), pos ({"x", "y"} on the board).
  • who is one of:
    • {"role": "Coder", "most": 2}: a role, with at most 1 to 5 agents;
    • {"team": "Web app"}: a team's stages;
    • {"lead": true}: the Orchestrator picks;
    • {"room": ["Coder", "Reviewer"]}: a room of 2 to 6 roles;
    • {"experts": "all"} (or "stale", "learned"): the team's experts;
    • {"candidates": "Coder", "most": 3, "target": 80, "models": "auto"}: 2 to 5 candidates; models is "auto", "same", or a list of {"provider_id", "model_id"}.
  • groups (at most 20): id, name, pos, wait (all or first). Steps join a group by its id.
  • ends (at most 10): id, then (in: take the work in; report: say what was found).
  • arrows (at most 200): {"from", "to"}.
  • loops (at most 20): {"from", "to", "rounds"}, going back, 1 to 5 rounds.

A recipe must start from start, reach an end on every path, and loop only backwards with a round limit. Only recipes kept in KOLONİ can be a team's default or picked for a chat.

items.title: Roles
items.text: Roles have no file format. You make and change them on the Agents page.

items.title: Skills
items.text:
A skill is a folder with a SKILL.md, in Claude Code's form:

---
name: my-skill
description: What it is for, in a sentence or two.
license: MIT
allowed-tools: Bash, Read
---

Instructions for the agent.
  • name (required): letters, digits, ., _ and -, starting with a letter or digit, at most 64.
  • description: at most 1024 characters are kept.
  • license: used if the folder has no LICENSE or COPYING file.
  • allowed-tools: KOLONİ maps these to its groups of tools. A role that lacks them is shown, with a way to give them.
  • At most 200 files and 5 MiB in all; SKILL.md at most 256 KiB; a .zip at most 25 MiB. Secret files are not copied.

items.title: The folder's .koloni/
items.text:
Path What it is rules.md The project's rules (Memory page, at most 1500 characters). Every agent is told them. settings.json Where commands run and the web search order (see below). recipes/ Recipes kept in this folder. knowledge/ Knowledge topics: each one's guide; the pages read are kept out of git. shared/ Files teams share while they work; kept out of git. tmp/ The agents' scratch space; kept out of git.

settings.json holds only these keys:

{
  "exec_location": "docker",
  "docker_image": "python:3.12",
  "docker_network": false,
  "search_order": "builtin"
}

exec_location is host or docker; search_order is builtin or cli. Other keys are ignored. Settings that came from another machine are shown to you before they are used (Use them / Not now).

items.title: Glossary
items.text:
KOLONİ's own words, as they appear on screen.

Agent One worker in a turn: a role running on a model. The canvas draws each agent as a small box: its name and model, its state, and what it did. Its tools, commands and files are in the Inspector. Agents may use A switch for each model on the Models page. When it is on, agents may pick that model by themselves, not only you. Always run A button on a command's card. It keeps a rule for that chat, so the same kind of command runs without a card next time. See Permission levels. Assistant PO After a turn that did something, one small model request with no tools that suggests at most three follow-up tasks for the To-do list, each with the words it came from. On the canvas it is a small box under the turn. See Follow-up tasks. Board A page with every chat of the project in three columns: at work, waiting for you, and done today. Branch (a team's) A git branch koloni/<name> that the Orchestrator can give a team's work. Stopped, the agent's work stays committed there; told to go on, it goes on on the same branch. The card offers Merge or Open pull request. See Branches. Candidates A recipe step given to several agents at once, each in its own working copy. Each one's work is scored from 0 to 100 by the project's Measure command, and the best one is kept. Card A box in the chat that waits for your answer, for example "Run this command?" with Run once, Always run … and Reject. There are cards for file changes, commands, web searches, secret files, opening a sub-agent, plans and more. Compare Compare… under More next to the message box. One message goes to two models side by side, each in its own working copy. Nothing reaches your project until you keep one. Coordinator A team's own lead, shown as "Team coordinator". It runs its team's stages and reports to the Orchestrator. Core The facts in a project's memory: what you approved or wrote yourself. See Memory. Decided for you Where you see the questions the Orchestrator answered while you were away, if you let it (Settings › This project › Asking and away › When you're away). Discussion Several agents talking one question through in rounds, with nobody changing anything meanwhile. An agent starts one; it has a token budget. Fact A short piece of memory that you approved or wrote, usually pointing to lines of a file. It is given to an agent whose task names its subject. Journal The notes in a project's memory: what agents wrote while they worked. Agents find notes only when they look. Knowledge A page of expert topics, each read once from web pages or project files into pages and a guide. Roles that know a topic use it while they work. MCP server A program on your machine that gives agents more tools. You add it on the Tools page, under Servers. Each tool asks before it runs unless you say otherwise. Measure command A command, set under Settings › This project › Checks and git, whose last line of output is a score from 0 to 100. It scores candidates. Memory What a project remembers between chats: your preferences, the project's rules, facts and notes. See Memory. Note A piece of memory an agent wrote with its Remember tool. See Memory. Observer A built-in role that never works on its own. If you switch on Have a model look over each sub-agent's report, its model reads each sub-agent's report and says what the record shows. Its words are an opinion, not a fact. Orchestrator The agent you talk to in a chat. It does small jobs itself and hands separate parts of the work to sub-agents. (Behind the scenes its role is named Lead.) Outside content Text that comes from outside your messages: web pages and searches, MCP tools' results, Knowledge pages and GitHub issues. KOLONİ frames it as data, not instructions, for the agents. See Outside content. Page key A secret that the KOLONİ page sends with every request, so that a program on your machine cannot approve cards or change settings in your place. It changes each time KOLONİ starts. Open KOLONİ from the link in its window. Part In the project map, a folder with its own project file (such as pyproject.toml or package.json), with its language and test command. In a recipe drawing, a step or a group of steps. Permission level What agents may do without asking: Ask before changes, Auto-edit files or Full auto. See Permission levels. Plain chat A chat with no folder ("No folder · a plain chat"). It is only talk: no files and no commands. Plan first A switch next to the message box. Each new message first gets a plan to approve before anything changes. Project A folder your agents work in. Each project has its own settings, memory and To-do list. Project notes A Knowledge topic that KOLONİ fills from what you tick on the Add to Project notes? card at the end of a turn. Provider Where a model runs: an OpenAI-compatible server, the Anthropic API, or a CLI you are signed in to (Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot CLI, Qoder, agy). You add providers on the Models page. Ready A page on the rail that lists everything waiting for your word, with a count. Ready for you The panel and page that list everything waiting for your word, in three parts: Needs your answer, Ready to take in and Told you. Recipe The drawn steps of a piece of work: who does each step, what runs at once, where it loops back and how it ends. Recipes are on the Agents page. Role What an agent is for: a description, instructions, the tools it may use and, if you like, its own model. KOLONİ comes with built-in roles such as Planner, Coder, Tester, Reviewer, Researcher, Debugger, Architect and Docs writer. You can add your own. Room Two to six agents working on one goal at the same time, in one working copy. They share the work out first, and each file has one holder. You open one with Work together… under More. Skill A folder with a SKILL.md and its files, in the form Claude Code reads. You add skills on the Tools page and give them to roles. Stop everything The button in the top bar that stops every turn in every chat and holds triggers, To-do lists that run by themselves, and work while you're away. While it holds, it reads Held · Resume. See Chat and canvas. Sub-agent An agent that the Orchestrator (or another agent) opens for a part of the work. It works in its own working copy. Take in Bringing finished work from a working copy into your project. Every card that does this says Take in. Team A named group of roles with stages: Plan, Build, Check, and Write & keep up. A chat can work with teams, picked under Teams for this chat: Orchestrator decides, Manual or No teams. Teams' work is ready The card where a recipe's work ends. It asks whether to take the work into the project, with Take in, Fix the findings and Ask for changes. Thinking How hard a role's model thinks, set on its Model card: Auto (the agent that opens it picks a level for each task, up to a most) or One fixed level, on a ladder from Off to Max. See Roles. Tier How strong you say a model is: fast, balanced or strongest. You set it for each model on the Models page. A model with no tier is never picked by itself. To-do A project's tasks, in your order. Agents, and the Assistant PO after a turn, propose tasks; you decide. Trigger Something that starts a turn by itself: the clock, a change to the project's files, or a request from outside (a webhook). Nobody watches such a turn, so it may do only what the trigger allows. Turn Everything that happens for one message: the Orchestrator's answer, the agents it opened, their tools, commands and changes. The canvas draws one turn at a time. Where the work is The panel the git button in the top bar opens ("⑂ main · 4 changed"): your branch, the agents' copies in this chat, and other branches, each saying how the work stands. See Branches. Workspace The side window with the project's files, what agents changed, wrote or showed, and what waits for you. Working copy A copy of your project, outside your folder, where a sub-agent makes its changes. Its work comes back to you on a card to take in or discard.

items.title: How a CLI runs
items.text:
A CLI provider has a setting How it runs:

On screen What it means One session per agent, with KOLONİ's tools (recommended) One CLI session per agent, using KOLONİ's tools. One run per model step, with KOLONİ's tools The CLI runs once for each model step: slower, and the answer arrives all at once. Native: its own tools, in the project The CLI uses its own tools in your folder and asks KOLONİ before each one. Reads with its own tools; started without leave to write or run agy only: it reads with its own tools and cannot change anything.

items.title: Known limits
items.text: What KOLONİ does not do yet, or does only in part.

items.title: First release (alpha)
items.text: Version 0.1.0 is the first release, an alpha: expect rough edges. Several paths were built against stand-ins only, including the Server tab for llama.cpp, Copilot with a GitHub token, and some limit and credit messages.

items.title: Secrets
items.text:
• A command that names a secret file, or searches the whole folder when the folder holds one (grep -r, rg, gci | gc), is asked about at every level, Full auto too. A script that opens a secret file without naming it (it builds the name, say) is not caught. Only Docker and Copilot's sandbox hide secret files from commands; KOLONİ's own commands on this machine, Claude Code, Codex, Qoder and agy do not.
  • When it runs Native, Codex runs the commands its own rules count as safe (a read of .env, or of a file outside the project) without asking KOLONİ, at every level; KOLONİ records them after they ran, so no card stands in their way. agy reading with its own tools has no hook: its reads, of a secret file too, are not asked about at any level. That Qoder asks before every tool is not yet measured.
  • A command you approve can still print, encode or send a secret it was given.
  • An agent's request for a key on a hidden card is not available to CLIs working with their own tools.
  • A branch deleted because it held a secret you gave still has its commits in git's reflog until git prunes them.

items.title: Outside content
items.text:
• Text from the web, MCP tools, Knowledge and GitHub issues is framed as data, but the frame only tells the model; a model can still follow what it says.
  • Only KOLONİ's own tools frame what they bring in. A CLI's own web fetch, MCP servers or file reads are not framed.
  • A forged end of the frame is not caught when it is written with look-alike letters from other scripts, with full-width or mathematical letters, with words joined by marks (end-of-the, end_of_the), or with markdown or HTML inside it. See Security model.

items.title: CLIs
items.text:
• When a CLI runs Native, it runs its commands itself, so its model reads their raw output; KOLONİ masks keys only in what it records and shows. Measured once on Copilot (Native) with a made-up GitHub token (ghp_…) in a command's output: it was *** in the model's answer and absent from Copilot's raw stream, so Copilot hid that kind of key itself; other kinds of key were not tried. Claude Code, Codex, Qoder and agy run Native were not measured. With KOLONİ's tools (as a session, or one run per step), the keys KOLONİ knows and values shaped or named like keys are masked before the model reads the output.
  • Copilot does not report which paths its PowerShell commands touch, so at Full auto a command that writes a protected file without naming it (a script, a path it builds) runs without a card. The same goes for KOLONİ's own commands at Full auto: one that names the file (echo … > .claude/settings.json) is asked about, but a script that writes ~/.claude/settings.json is not. Such a file in the project is put back, and you are asked whether to keep it; one outside the project is not.
  • Claude Code, Qoder and agy run Native (and Copilot where it cannot sandbox its commands) have no sandbox of KOLONİ's: it can stop what they do only at their hook. A write with their own file tools outside the project and the folders it also works in (or that you allowed) is asked about on a card at every level, Full auto too, and refused in a turn nobody watches (in a working copy, refused: it may write only in the copy); one into a CLI's own folder (.claude, .gemini, .codex or .copilot in your home folder) or another place KOLONİ never opens (.ssh, browser profiles) is refused. Their commands are judged by what they name: a command that writes outside the project, for example to the Startup folder or a PowerShell profile, runs without a card at Full auto, and at any level where an allow rule covers it, unless it names a CLI's settings folder such as .claude or .gemini, or a secret file, or it deletes or sends data off the machine.
  • Claude Code and Qoder run Native do not say where their commands run, so KOLONİ judges each one as run in the project folder. If the CLI keeps a cd from an earlier command, later relative paths are judged at the wrong place: after you approve cd .., reading a file there by its name is taken for a read in the project and is not asked about below Full auto. Whether Claude Code keeps a cd that leaves the project is not measured.
  • A sub-agent on Claude Code or Qoder run Native works in a working copy, but its commands are not sandboxed: at Full auto, one that writes into your project by a path it does not spell out (..\.., a script) changes the project directly. KOLONİ finds such a change at the end of the turn and records it as made in the project by an unknown maker.
  • Triggers do not start a turn on a CLI that works with its own tools (Native, or agy).
  • GitHub Copilot CLI's tokens and AI credits run as a session are counted from its usage checkpoint, as in Native; measured with copilot -p (CLI 1.0.103), not yet seen in a live session.
  • Copilot's thinking levels on a model server of your own are not measured.
  • An agy model whose name ends in its level takes no other level. Only a name ending in -low was seen to refuse one; the other endings are read the same way, not measured.

items.title: GitHub
items.text: • Reading a GitHub issue with a real gh is not measured yet: the fields KOLONİ asks gh for are taken from gh's manual.

items.title: Models
items.text: • Other OpenAI-compatible servers, such as Ollama, should work but are not tested. The local server that is measured is llama.cpp's llama-server.

items.title: Commands
items.text:
• Some harmful commands are not on the list yet: kubectl delete, terraform destroy, rsync --delete, robocopy /MIR, mail, ssh host 'command'.
  • At Full auto, the harm check sees honest commands only; a command written to hide what it does is not seen. See Security model.
  • Commands cannot be given input while they run.
  • In Docker on Linux and macOS, commands run as your user, not as root. A command that needs root in the container, such as apt-get install, fails. On Linux, files an older version of KOLONİ made as root in the project may no longer be writable; see Troubleshooting. Under rootless Docker, the files a command makes belong to another user id on the host.

items.title: Recipes
items.text:
• Recipes do not run in triggers' turns.
  • A chat cannot open a room while a recipe runs.
  • A team as a step's "Who" runs its stages as slots of one step, not one after another.

items.title: The page
items.text:
• Canvas positions are worked out from the record each time and are not saved.
  • At phone width, the top bar wraps to two lines.
  • Desktop notifications are on Windows only.

items.title: Systems
items.text: macOS, Linux and the Docker image have been tested less than Windows. See Install.

items.title: HTTP API
items.text: KOLONİ's page talks to KOLONİ through an HTTP API under /api, on 127.0.0.1. The API is made for the page; it is not a public interface and may change between versions.

items.title: The page key
items.text:
Every /api request must carry the page key, in the X-KOLONI-Key header (or ?key= for event streams and downloads). Without it the answer is 401: "open KOLONİ from the link in its window". The key is in the link KOLONİ prints at the start, after #key=.

A few doors need no key:

  • GET /api/health;
  • POST /api/hooks/{key}: a trigger's webhook, with its own key in the address, from this machine only;
  • POST /api/limits/claude-session: Claude Code's status line;
  • POST /api/open: swapping the one-time code for the key;
  • the frames that show files and views.

items.title: The schema
items.text:
KOLONİ does not serve API docs or its OpenAPI schema. To get the schema, run, from KOLONİ's folder:

.venv/Scripts/python.exe scripts/export_openapi.py openapi.json

It builds the app with a temporary data folder and writes its OpenAPI description. The page's own types (frontend/src/api/generated.ts) are generated from it with npm run generate:api in frontend/.

items.title: What happens when you upgrade
items.text:
1. Back up first. The update script backs the database up to runtime/data/backups/ before it pulls the new version. For more, use Settings › The app › Your data › Export everything.
  2. Update: stop KOLONİ, then run ./scripts/update.ps1 (Windows) or ./scripts/update.sh. See Backup and update.
  3. Start KOLONİ again. If the new version changes the database, KOLONİ copies it to runtime/data/backups/ and then upgrades it. It keeps the last five copies there, the update script's included.

If something goes wrong, the copies in runtime/data/backups/ are whole databases. Stop KOLONİ before you put one back in place of runtime/data/koloni.db.

items.title: Version by version
items.text: No version has been released yet. Changes that need your attention will be listed here, and in the Changelog.

items.title: Security model
items.text:
KOLONİ lets agents read, change and run things on your machine. This page says what stands in their way, and where that ends.

Security boundaries at a glance; each is explained below.

items.title: The short version
items.text:
• Ask before changes and Auto-edit files are the wall. Below Full auto, every command that is not plain read-only work waits for your card, unless a rule you made covers it, and rules cover only simple commands.
  • Full auto runs commands without asking. Its check for harmful commands (deleting, force-pushing, sending data off the machine) is a courtesy for honest commands, not a wall: a command written to hide what it does is not seen. Use Full auto only for work you are ready to let run.
  • For a wall against a deliberate attacker on your own account, run agents' commands in Docker, or run KOLONİ as another user.

items.title: The page key
items.text:
Every request to KOLONİ's API must carry the page key. So a program on your machine, such as a command an agent runs, cannot approve its own cards or change your settings. Agents never get the key: KOLONİ takes it out of its own environment, hides it in output, and opens your browser with a one-time code instead. Requests must also come to 127.0.0.1 or localhost.

The key does not stop a program that deliberately goes after it as your own user (for example, by reading your browser's files). See Install.

items.title: Cards and rules
items.text:
Permission levels lists what asks at each level. A rule you make with Always run covers only a plain command. A rule never covers:

  • a command that is chained, piped, redirected, or handed to a shell or another program;
  • a command that deletes or cannot be undone;
  • a command that names a secret file, .koloni/, or a file that steers agents;
  • git:
    • only common git commands can have a rule (such as git status, git diff, git log, git commit); others, such as git archive or git difftool, ask every time;
    • never the bare git rule, and never an option before git's command (git -c …);
    • never an option that makes git run a program or write a file it is told of (git grep -O…, --upload-pack, --exec, --output, --config and the like), even under a rule;
  • downloads (curl, wget, Invoke-WebRequest): a rule only fetches. It never covers writing a file (-o, -O, -OutFile), reading options from a file (-K, --config), sending data, or a file: address.

items.title: Places agents never open
items.text:
• Your home folder, a drive's root and KOLONİ's own folder cannot be opened as a project. Settings › The app › Your data › Always blocked lists the places no agent ever opens: where your secrets are kept, KOLONİ itself and the system's folders.
